source.author: 枯白 Kubai
source.title: 999 个小技巧 · 004：嵌套圆角与连续圆角
source.verification: 已通过 FxTwitter 逐条读取原帖文本

entries.summary: 为卡片、面板和控件约定圆角；遇到等距嵌套，再按间距计算内层半径。
entries.definition: 当一个圆角容器包住另一个元素时，内层圆角应随内缩距离变小。对于等距内缩的普通圆角，内圆角 r = 外圆角 R − 间距 p。这样转角处的留白才会与直边处一样均匀。
entries.when: 表单、嵌套面板、图片容器，以及带有内层按钮的卡片。
steps: 先从项目的圆角变量中选取容器半径，再按内缩距离计算内层圆角。
例如外层 32px、间距 12px，内层使用 20px。
R 小于 p 时用 0 作为下限；圆形、胶囊形和不同形状需要单独判断。
entries.avoid: 给所有层级套同一个大圆角。这个公式适用于等距内缩的圆弧，不能直接保证所有超椭圆轮廓的等距。
entries.prompt:
Make the corner radii in this UI consistent, then switch them to continuous corners. Work on the screen or components I name; ask me if I have not named them. If the project has radius tokens, change those instead of hard-coding values.

Inner radius = outer radius - padding (r = R - p)
Go from the outside in: dialog or card -> panels, inputs, buttons -> chips and tags. A box p inside a container with radius R gets R - p, so both corners share one center. Example: dialog 32, padding 16 -> panels and buttons 16; a chip 8 inside a 16 panel -> 8.
Boxes on the same level share one radius. Never go below 4.

Pills and circles stay fully round.
Keep every padding, gap and radius on a 4px grid.
Continuous corners
Keep border-radius and add the curve as progressive enhancement: @ supports (corner-shape: superellipse(1.25)) { :where(*) { corner-shape: superellipse(1.25); } } Set corner-shape: round on pills and circles.

Chrome and Edge 139+ render it; Safari and Firefox skip the block and show the plain border-radius.
When done, list every radius you changed as "element: old -> new".

entries.summary: 为颜色、间距和圆角命名，让设计拥有共同的词汇。
entries.definition: Design Token 是具有名字的设计决策，例如 surface、text-muted、space-4。组件引用名字，而不是各自写一套数值。修改一个语义变量，可以让相关组件保持一致。Kubai 的分层示例先区分浅色与深色的色板，再让组件引用按用途命名的颜色。
entries.when: 同一种颜色、间距或状态在多个组件里反复出现时。
steps: 先收集界面中实际重复的值。
区分原始数值与用途名称，例如紫色与主要操作色。
让组件引用用途名称，再检查交互状态是否完整。
entries.avoid: 只把每一个硬编码数值改成变量，却仍然留下数十个含义相同的名字。
entries.prompt:
1. 使用组件化管理的思路处理 UI 组件，建立样式与色彩的变量体系，形成 Design Token，保证风格连续。

2. 参考业界成熟的组件库构建组件库的语义体系，建立 Do /Don't 范例，根据正确的语义和场景选择组件，修正当前产品中不合适的组件。

3. 使用全局变量统一管理圆角，使用等距内缩体系。如条件可行且性能无忧，使用连续圆角。

4. 建立全局间距体系，使用 4 的倍数。根据语义的逻辑嵌套关系分配元素间的间距。元素嵌套时，保证必要场景下上下左右间距一致。

5. 移除不必要的 UX 文案。先明确当前页面定位，保留核心标题，关键键值对文案。说明文字符合书面表达规范，避免营销或口语化。根据用户可能的使用频率，在形式上采用 tooltip、alert 等方式作折叠，不必常驻显示。

entries.summary: 用真实世界的光、边缘和材质，解释一个数字物件。
entries.definition: 拟物设计借用实体物件的外观线索，让数字界面具有可感知的材质和层次。本站从 Kubai 对 Portrait 界面的点评出发，演示描边、浅渐变和光影怎样共同建立体积。
entries.when: 需要触感的播放器、工具按钮、仪表或具有鲜明性格的小型界面。
steps: 先确定统一光源，所有明暗遵守同一方向。
用细描边明确边界，用低强度渐变交代曲面。
保留足够的文字对比度，让操作含义优先于装饰。
entries.avoid: 每个元素都使用厚重投影和高光，造成多个互相冲突的光源。
entries.prompt: 为指定控件增加克制的拟物质感。沿用现有尺寸和语义，统一上方光源，用细边缘、轻微表面渐变与接触阴影区分层次。给出普通、按下和键盘焦点状态。

entries.summary: 在设计规范里约定哪些组件使用连续圆角，让同类组件在各页面保持相同的轮廓。
entries.definition: 普通圆角由直线接圆弧，连接处的曲率会发生跳变。连续圆角通过不同的曲线形状缓和这个变化。超椭圆是构建这类柔和轮廓的一种方法，并不代表任意参数都具备相同效果。
entries.when: 应用图标、大型面板和需要柔和轮廓的容器。
steps: 先约定采用连续圆角的组件，例如大面板；这些组件共用同一曲线，并保留普通圆角作为回退。
对照 Mark Davis 的曲线示例，沿轮廓观察直线接入弯角的位置。实现时用 @supports 检测 corner-shape。
在目标浏览器检查实际轮廓，圆形和胶囊仍保留 round。
entries.avoid: 把特定浏览器版本的兼容结论当作永久事实。本站用运行时能力检测，并展示明确的回退状态。

entries.definition: 间距体系是一组有限、重复使用的距离。4px 可以作为基础单位，但真正决定距离的是信息之间的关系：标签和输入框更近，两组表单更远，页面章节之间最远。

结合文字行高检查视觉留白，而不是只看盒模型。

entries.summary: 状态变了，用户仍然知道自己刚刚操作了什么。
entries.definition: 界面连续性让用户在状态切换时保留对元素身份、位置和关系的理解。例如按钮展开成菜单时，菜单从触发位置生长出来，比远处突然出现一个面板更容易追踪。Kubai 在教程演示中保留了光标。镜头快速切换时，观看者可以跟着指针找到下一处操作。
entries.when: 菜单、抽屉、手风琴、详情展开，以及其他会改变空间关系的交互。
steps: 识别状态变化前后仍然属于同一个对象的元素。
菜单在按钮下方打开时，让缩放原点靠近按钮。若菜单翻到按钮上方，原点也移到菜单下缘。
检查周围内容的变化，并提供减少动态效果的版本。
entries.avoid: 把所有出现和消失都处理成淡入淡出，或者为了过渡延迟用户操作。
entries.prompt:
Find the places in my product where the interface jumps from one state to the next, and make the important ones continuous: the element I touched should carry into what comes next instead of disappearing and being replaced. First diagnose and suggest; build only what I pick.

This is a change to my product, not a demo. Work inside my code, on my stack, with my components, tokens and layout. Keep what every action does, what each screen shows and where things end up; change only how one state becomes the next. Do not copy a demo scene (no phone frame, backdrop, sample content or fonts). Do not add a dependency or a router change without asking. Every value below is a default to start from. It applies to phone and desktop layouts alike; section 3 says where they differ.

0. Read the product first
- Find the screens, routes, panels, sheets, dialogs, menus and lists, and how one opens from another: navigation stack or router, modal and sheet presenters, popover and menu components, list and grid components.
- Find what animates today and how: CSS transitions, the View Transitions API, Motion or Framer Motion, GSAP, SwiftUI or UIKit transitions, Compose animations, Flutter Hero or implicit animations. Note the motion tokens (durations, curves, springs) and reduced-motion handling, and reuse them.
- Note which layouts exist (phone, tablet, desktop window, split view) and the input on each (touch, mouse, keyboard).
- Tell me in a few lines what you found before going on.

1. What to look for
A jump is where I act on one element and the next state appears from nowhere: a hard cut, a cross-fade of whole screens, or something sliding in from an unrelated edge. Look for these, the most common first:
a. A row or item opens its detail page. Continuous: the row's title grows into the page title; its picture into the header; the previous page's title shrinks into the back button. When the page scrolls, the large title tucks into the top bar, centred on the control row. Going back reverses all of it.
b. A card opens into a full view or a dialog. Continuous: the card itself grows into the view (its frame, corners and picture), its title stays the same line of type and only scales, and the rest fades in once the card is mostly open. Closing, or dragging it down, shrinks it back into the same card in the same place.
c. A compact bar opens into a full panel: a mini player, a chat bubble, an upload or download pill, a toast with details. Continuous: the bar is the panel; its cover, title and main button grow into their places in it. The panel stays opaque all the way, and the page behind steps back (scale about 0.94, dimmed about 30%).
d. Search or filter. Continuous: the field moves up into the top row as the page title leaves and a Cancel or close slides in; while typing, the matching items slide from where they are to their place in the results and the rest fade out. On desktop the same applies to a command palette opening from its field.
e. A summary opens into its detail: a metric tile into a chart, a progress ring into a report, a thumbnail into a gallery. Continuous: the small marks become the large ones (the sparkline is the chart's line, the small bars are the chart's bars), the label moves into the title, and the number scales up rather than being redrawn.
f. A control opens what it controls: a ⋯ or + button into its menu or form, a select into its list, a date field into its picker. Continuous: the panel grows out of the control from the control's own corner, its items fade in after it is mostly open (about 25ms apart), and the highlight slides from item to item with the pointer or finger. When an action adds, removes or moves something, it appears in its place and the others move to make room; nothing jumps.
g. Tabs, segmented controls, bottom bars and side navigation. Continuous: one indicator travels from the old tab to the new one. Its leading edge leaves first and the trailing edge follows, so it stretches on the way and settles as it lands (a small squash of about 15% of its height at the longest is enough); labels collapse and expand while the other items make room. New content enters from the side of the tab that was chosen.
h. Layout changes: grid to list, sort, reorder, insert, delete, expand and collapse. Continuous: each item moves from where it was to where it goes; items that change row leave at the end of their row and come in at the start of the next, so nothing crosses the grid.

2. How to make it continuous
- One element, not two. The thing that moves is the same element (or a shared element the framework matches by id), measured where it starts and where it ends. Animate between the two boxes with transforms; never animate width, height, top or margin on things that reflow.
- What only one state has fades: content that exists only at the end fades in after about 45-55% of the move, and content that exists only at the start fades out in the first 25-35%. Text that changes size scales; it is not cross-faded with a copy.
- Keep layers honest: a panel that grows is opaque all the way, so nothing shows through it; the moving element stays above its neighbours while it moves, and goes back to its place in the stack when it lands.
- Shapes keep their corners: the radius changes smoothly between start and end, using the product's own corner curve. Nested shapes keep equal padding and concentric corners.
- Timing: open and close with a fast start and a long settle, cubic-bezier(.32, .72, 0, 1) or the product's own spring. Phones: 450-700ms for something that becomes a full screen, 350-500ms for menus and sheets, 400-450ms for an indicator. Desktop: about two thirds of that, and shorter still when it was triggered from the keyboard. Moves within a screen use ease-in-out. Staggers stay between 20 and 50ms.
- Gestures: while a finger or the pointer drags, follow it 1:1 (a dragged card shrinks to about 0.82 as it goes); on release, finish with the release velocity, toward whichever end is nearer.
- Interruptions: a new action takes over from wherever the animation is; nothing waits for an animation to finish, and input is never blocked.
- Reduced motion: keep the change of state and a short cross-fade (about 150ms), drop the movement and scaling.
- Accessibility: focus moves to the new state's heading or first control, and back to the element that opened it when it closes; screen readers announce the new state as they do now.

3. Phone and desktop
- Phone: everything above, with gestures (swipe back, drag to dismiss) driving the same animation as the buttons, and safe areas respected at every frame.
- Desktop: the same patterns, smaller and quicker. A card or row usually opens into a side panel or dialog rather than a full window; grow it from the card into that panel. Do not zoom whole windows. Hover never starts a layout animation. Keep pointer targets in place while they animate, so a second click lands where it aims. In split views, animate inside the pane that changes.
- Window resizing and responsive breakpoints are not transitions; do not animate them.

4. Report before building
Go through the product and give me a ranked list, at most 10 entries, each with:
- Where: the screen or component, and the action that triggers it (on phone, desktop or both).
- Now: what happens today, in one line.
- Pattern: which of a-h it is, and which element should carry over.
- Change: what moves to where, the duration and curve, in two or three lines.
- Value: high, medium or low, from how often people do it and how lost they could get without it.
- Cost: what has to change in the code, and any risk (routing, virtualized lists, shared state).
Put the frequent, disorienting ones with low cost first. Then ask me which ones to build and wait.

5. Build what I pick
- Describe the approach for each on my platform (section 6 is a starting point), and list the files you will touch. Wait for my go-ahead.
- Build them one at a time. For each, list the files you touched, and check:
  - The first and last frame match the real states exactly; nothing jumps when the moving element hands over to the real one.
  - Real data: long and short text, missing images, the first and last item, an empty list, a scrolled list.
  - Fast repeated taps or clicks, going back during the animation, and gestures cancelled half way.
  - Phone and desktop layouts, light and dark, reduced motion, keyboard and screen reader.
  - At rest every screen looks exactly as before, and existing tests still pass.

6. How, by platform (check against my versions)
- Web: the View Transitions API with view-transition-name on the shared elements (same-document, and cross-document where pages are separate), with a plain update as the fallback. Otherwise FLIP: measure first, apply the change, measure last, animate the inverse with transforms (Motion's layout and layoutId do this; so do Svelte's flip and crossfade, and Vue's TransitionGroup). For router-driven pages, start the transition from the router's navigation hook.
- iOS: SwiftUI matchedGeometryEffect for shared elements in one view, navigationTransition(.zoom(sourceID:in:)) with matchedTransitionSource on iOS 18 and later for pushes and sheets; UIKit preferredTransition = .zoom on iOS 18, or a custom UIViewControllerAnimatedTransitioning with UIViewPropertyAnimator for interruptible, gesture-driven ones.
- Android: Compose SharedTransitionLayout with Modifier.sharedElement and sharedBounds, AnimatedContent, Modifier.animateItem for lists, and predictive back for gesture-driven returns; with Views, MaterialContainerTransform and shared element transitions.
- Flutter: Hero for shared elements between routes, OpenContainer from the animations package for card to page, AnimatedList and implicit animations for layout changes.
- Desktop apps: Electron and Tauri take the web route (Tauri uses the system WebView, so test View Transitions there and keep the fallback); native apps use the same ideas with their own animation tools.

entries.summary: 告诉用户「刚才的操作有结果了」，然后轻轻离开。
entries.definition: Toast 是与当前操作紧密相关的短暂反馈，例如复制完成。它通常自动消失，可以附带撤销入口。对用户必须处理的问题，应使用持续可见的提示，而不是让信息随 Toast 一起消失。
entries.when: 保存完成、复制成功，以及无需持续处理的操作结果。
steps: 用一句简短文案明确发生了什么。
非紧急反馈通过 status 区域礼貌播报。

  b. Action: the action has already been done, and the toast holds the one step that may follow, usually Undo. One line and one button, plus a close. It stays long enough to use the button, with the time left shown.
  c. Progress: work that takes a moment. It shows that the work is under way, then turns into the result in the same place, with a button to see it. Example: "Uploading brand-guide.pdf" turns into "Uploaded to Files, Open".
- Notification: news the person did not cause just now, from other people or from the system: a mention, a reply, a payment, a deadline, a security alert, a finished report. It can carry more: a title, a few lines and up to two actions. It is shown on every page, stays until it is opened, handled or closed, and several can be shown at once. It is also kept somewhere the person can find it again (an inbox or a list behind a bell, with a count).
- Neither:
  - A form error or a problem with one field: show it next to the field.
  - A failure the person has to fix (an upload that failed, a payment that did not go through): keep it on the item, with a way to fix it, until it is fixed. A toast that disappears after a few seconds is not enough.
  - An action that cannot be undone: ask before doing it (a confirm next to the button, or a dialog for something with a large impact). A toast after the fact is too late.
  - Something only worth seeing when the person looks: a badge, a dot or a change of state in place, with no message at all.

2. Questions that settle a case
- Who caused it? The person, just now: toast. Someone else, the system, or the person a while ago in another place: notification.
- Does the person need to act? No: status toast. One quick step that may follow (Undo, View): action toast. A real decision or a reply: notification. Something that must be fixed: keep it on the item.
- Can the action be undone? Then do it at once and offer Undo in a toast instead of asking first. If it cannot be undone, confirm before, not after.
- How much is there to say? A few words: toast. A sentence or two, a name, an amount, a place: notification.
- Would it matter if the person missed it? No: toast. Yes: notification, kept until handled.
- Is the work still running when the person leaves? If it ends while they are still on the page, a toast is enough. - Several at once? Toasts: one at a time; a new one replaces the old one, or waits. Notifications: they stack.

- Where: the screen or component, and what triggers it.

- Why: one line, using the questions above.
- Change: what would change (kind, wording, buttons, how long it stays, where it is kept).

C. Both.

- Place: the top centre of the page, 12 under the top bar, over the content. One at a time.
- Shape: 40 tall, 16 corners (or the nearest step in my corner scale), a white surface with a soft top-to-bottom gradient (#ffffff to #f7f9fc), a 1px border rgba(214, 219, 227, 0.95), and a soft shadow (0 16px 36px rgba(17, 24, 39, 0.08), 0 3px 10px rgba(17, 24, 39, 0.05)). - Leave: 220ms, ease-in: up 6px, blur 6px, fade out.
- Sheen: a light band crosses it once (900ms, ease-out) only when something is done: a status toast as it enters, a progress toast as it turns into its result, an Undo toast after Undo. An action toast that still waits for a choice enters without it.
- Change in place (progress to result, archived to restored): the old line (text, button and close together) blurs out and moves 5px up in 180ms; the new line blurs in from 5px below between 100 and 400ms; the toast takes its new width in 380ms on cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1). - After Undo: the change is reverted, and the toast says so ("Task restored") for about 1.5 seconds before it leaves.
- Timing: a status toast stays 3 to 5 seconds, longer for longer text; an action toast at least 5 seconds; a progress toast stays while the work runs, then 3 seconds. The timer pauses while the pointer is over the toast or focus is inside it.

4B. Notifications
- Place: the top right, 12 under the top bar, the same on every page, above the content. 344 wide.
- Card: 24 corners with 12 of padding, so the picture (32, a person's photo or the product's logo) and the buttons (32 tall, 12 corners) are concentric with it. A title (14/20, semibold) with the time on the right, up to three lines of 13/20 text, then up to two buttons on the bottom right, the main one last.
- A stack: the newest is in front. The older ones are cut to the front one's height and peek out 12 below it, at 95% and 90%, showing only their edge; at most three show.
- A new one arrives: it slides down onto the stack from 56px above in 560ms on cubic-bezier(0.32, 0.72, 0, 1), clearing from a light blur, while the others are pushed down and back a step. - Close one, as on macOS: a small close button (24, 10 corners) appears over a card's top-left corner while the pointer is on that card. Handling a card with one of its buttons also removes it. - Counts: the bell shows how many are waiting, and so does the page title, so a tab in the background shows it too. Notifications that need a decision (security, payments) stay in the list behind the bell even when they are cleared from the screen.

- Reduced motion: keep the change of state and a short fade (about 150ms); drop the movement, scaling and blur.
- Screen readers: toasts are announced politely (role="status"); a notification that needs attention is announced once as it arrives. Neither takes focus away from what the person is doing. Their buttons can be reached by keyboard, and Escape closes the one in focus.
- Touch: the same places, with swipe to dismiss; there is no hover, so the stack spreads on tap.
- Dark mode: the same rules on my dark surfaces; the sheen is fainter.

- List the files you will touch and wait for my go-ahead.
- Change one thing at a time and keep what each action does. Then check:
  - Short and long text, a missing picture, many notifications at once, several toasts in a row.
  - Undo used, ignored and closed; a progress that fails; leaving the page while something is still running.
  - Phone and desktop layouts, light and dark, reduced motion, keyboard and screen reader.
  - Existing tests still pass.
- Web: CSS transitions or the Web Animations API for the toast; for the stack, measure each card's height and animate transform and height together. Sonner (React) has a similar stack and can be adapted, but ask before adding it. iOS, Android and Flutter: use the platform's own animation tools with the same values; for messages that reach people outside the app, use the system's notifications.

source.author: 枯白 Kubai
source.title: 999 个小技巧 · 018：镭射质感
source.verification: 已通过 FxTwitter 逐条读取原帖文本
source.note: 文本来自公开帖子预览。笔记解释由本站整理；提示词和媒体分别标注作者与出处。

entries.summary: 把角度变成颜色，让一张卡片像真实藏品。
entries.definition: 界面中的镭射效果通过随观察角度变化的色彩与高光，模拟全息箔材质。Kubai 的卡片案例把倾斜、亮边和深度层次组合在一起。
entries.when: 数字门票、纪念卡、收藏卡和需要被特别看见的物件。
steps: 先建立稳定的底色和清晰内容，再添加色彩层。
让高光跟随指针，控制倾斜幅度。
给触屏和键盘用户可用的替代交互，减少动态时保持静态。
entries.avoid: 让反光覆盖关键信息，或在大面积阅读区域持续自动晃动。
entries.prompt:
Turn a card in my product into a holographic card: it tilts toward the pointer in 3D, a foil finish and a glare follow the light across it, the artwork inside has depth, it sways a little when left alone, and (if I want) it turns over on click to show its back, with a visible edge. Build it inside my code and design system; do not change what the card says or does.

Every value in this prompt is a recommendation, not a requirement. Sections 1 to 7 give a full set that works together (the "Standard" values, tested in a demo); section 9 gives presets around them. I choose; you build what I choose.

First look at my product (section 0). Then ask me these one at a time. For each, show the options in a short list with their key values, mark the recommended one, and wait for my answer; I may pick an option, change single values, or give my own:
1. Which card: the one element that stands for status or ownership (a member or loyalty card, a ticket or pass, a badge or achievement, a profile or collectible card, a plan tier). Holographic effects lose their meaning when everything shines, so one card per screen.
2. Finish: one of the six in section 3 (Prism recommended), several to choose from (for tiers or rarity), or my brand colors (then derive the base, foil, glare, rim and edge from them and show me the values).
3. Feel: Quiet, Standard (recommended) or Lively (section 9), or my own tilt angle, springs and sway.
4. Interactions: tilt toward the pointer (on), the idle sway (on), turning over on click (needs a back: say what goes on it, such as a QR code or terms), tilting with the phone's motion on mobile (off; needs permission on iOS).
5. If it turns over: the thickness (Thin, Standard recommended, Thick) and the flip spring (section 9).
6. Depth: which parts of the card's artwork get their own layer, and how deep (None, Subtle, Standard recommended; section 9).
7. Background: leave the page behind the card as it is (recommended for most products), or add the slow fluid behind it (section 7).
Then sum up my choices with their values in one table, propose how you will build it on my platform (section 8 is a starting point), with the cost and any fallback, and wait for my go-ahead.

0. Start from what exists
- Find the card: its component, size, corner radius, artwork and content, where it sits, and what is around it. Check whether a back already exists (terms, a code, details).
- Find how the screen draws (DOM, a native view tree, a GPU renderer), the platform version range, whether there is a dark mode, and how pointer and touch input reach the card.
- Tell me in a few lines what you found before asking.

1. Tilt and light (Standard)
- With the pointer at (fx, fy) in 0..1 across the card, nx = fx * 2 - 1 and ny = fy * 2 - 1, the target is rotateY = nx * 12deg and rotateX = -ny * 12deg. Perspective 1600px on the card's parent.
- The tilt follows its target on a spring, so it overshoots a little when the pointer leaves: acceleration = 140 * (target - angle) - 15 * velocity, per second.
- The light sits where the pointer is (lx = fx * 100%, ly = fy * 100%) and follows on a spring without overshoot (stiffness 160, damping 2 * sqrt(160) ≈ 25.3). With no pointer on the card, it rests up and to the left (34%, 22%), like a lamp in the room.
- Hover strength `on` goes from 0 to 1 while the pointer is on the card, easing at 1 - exp(-7 * dt) per frame; it brightens the foil and the glare.
- Left alone, the card sways as if held: rotateX = 2.2deg * sin(0.9t + 0.6) + 0.8deg * sin(2.3t), rotateY = 3.2deg * sin(0.7t) + 0.9deg * sin(1.9t + 1.2), t in seconds, and the light moves with it (lx = 34% + rotateY * 3, ly = 22% - rotateX * 3).
- Touch: dragging on the card tilts it the same way (touch-action: none on the card only). Phone motion, if chosen, maps the device's tilt to the same target, clamped to the same angles.
- The shadow under the card: a blurred ellipse (black at 60%, blur 24px, 84% of the card's width, 70px tall, 30px below it) that slides away from the side that lifts: x = -rotateY * 1.8px, y = rotateX * 1.2px.

2. The layers of a face, back to front
- Art: the card's own base color or picture.
- Foil: the finish (section 3), blended over the art, brightest near the light.
- Print: everything printed on the card (text, logo, artwork window), above the foil so it stays readable.
- Glare: a radial gradient centered on the light, white at 60% in the middle, 14% at 28%, then black at 30% at 95% (farthest corner), blended with overlay; opacity 0.35 + on * 0.65.
- Rim: a 1.5px ring around the edge (mask with content-box exclude): a faint base color all round, plus a radial gradient at the light in the rim's light color, fading out by 42%; opacity 0.6 + on * 0.4. It should come and go as the card moves, never read as a solid outline.
- A hologram seal, if the card has a place for one: a 44px disc, conic-gradient(from <angle>, rgb(255 154 200), rgb(255 224 138), rgb(164 255 207), rgb(143 220 255), rgb(183 155 255), repeated twice), with fine rings over it (white at 35%, 1px every 3.5px) and a 1px white rim at 60%. The angle = atan2(ly - 50%, lx - 50%) * 1.5 + rotateY * 6.
- Corners: 32px on a 440 x 616 card (scale with the card), on a continuous curve where the platform has one.

3. Finishes (recommended values; pick, mix or derive from my brand)
Each lists: base, foil, glare and rim if they differ from section 2, ink, edge color (for the thickness), and the glow behind the card (section 7).
- Prism (recommended): deep blue glass lit from inside.
  - Base: radial-gradient(60% 40% at 50% 0%, rgb(90 150 255 / 0.55), transparent), linear-gradient(170deg, rgb(13 35 168), rgb(8 18 102) 55%, rgb(22 15 92)). Ink rgb(244 244 246).
  - The artwork window holds the light: radial-gradient(46% 50% at the light, rgb(255 175 235) at 0.55, 0.4 at 18%, 0.22 at 38%, 0.09 at 60%, 0.02 at 82%, transparent), radial-gradient(54% 56% at (100% - lx, 74%), rgb(125 225 255) at 0.45, 0.32 at 18%, 0.17 at 38%, 0.07 at 60%, 0.015 at 82%, transparent), radial-gradient(70% 55% at 30% 100%, rgb(150 255 210 / 0.3), transparent 75%), over linear-gradient(170deg, rgb(59 98 230), rgb(42 63 191) 55%, rgb(58 47 168)). Many stops, so it reads as glow, not spots. Its frame: rgb(140 170 255 / 0.1) with a 1px line at rgb(170 200 255 / 0.28).
  - Foil: a 2px lit rim, radial-gradient(at the light, rgb(170 220 255 / 0.9), transparent 60%), masked to the ring; opacity 0.15 + on * 0.45. Glare opacity 0.25 + on * 0.45.
  - Edge rgb(26 42 138). Glow hue 228.
- Rainbow: bands of color that slide as it tilts.
  - Base: radial-gradient(130% 80% at 25% 0%, rgb(59 62 76), rgb(27 28 35) 62%). Ink rgb(245 245 247).
  - Foil: repeating-linear-gradient(115deg, rgb(255 95 126) 0%, rgb(255 184 107) 2.6%, rgb(244 255 107) 5.2%, rgb(107 255 181) 7.8%, rgb(95 210 255) 10.4%, rgb(139 123 255) 13%, rgb(255 107 214) 15.6%, rgb(255 95 126) 18%), background-size 200%, background-position at the light, under a grating repeating-linear-gradient(125deg, transparent 0 2px, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3) 2px 3px); mix-blend-mode color-dodge, filter brightness(0.72) saturate(1.25), opacity 0.3 + on * 0.6, masked by radial-gradient(farthest-corner at the light, rgb(0 0 0) 5%, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.16) 72%).
  - Edge rgb(42 44 53). Glow hue 285.
- Pearl: a white card with a pastel sheen, strongest toward its edges like a frame.
  - Base: linear-gradient(160deg, rgb(253 252 255), rgb(241 238 248)). Ink rgb(23 21 46).
  - Foil: linear-gradient(115deg, rgb(255 196 225) 0%, rgb(201 184 255) 12%, rgb(180 233 255) 24%, rgb(194 255 216) 36%, rgb(255 243 184) 48%, then the same again), background-size 260%, position at the light, multiply, opacity 0.7 + on * 0.3, masked by radial-gradient(70% 60% at 50% 45%, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.35) 30%, rgb(0 0 0) 100%).
  - Glare: soft-light, white at 90% fading out by 55%, opacity 0.5 + on * 0.5. Rim: base rgb(60 50 120 / 0.06), light white at 95%.
  - Edge rgb(230 226 242). Glow hue 300.
- Sparkle: fine glitter.
  - Base: radial-gradient(120% 80% at 75% 5%, rgb(40 51 106), rgb(16 20 43) 65%). Ink rgb(238 240 255).
  - Glitter: a 240px tile of about 950 dots, radius 0.45 to 1.85px (most small), alpha 0.35 to 1, used as an alpha mask.
  - Foil, blended with screen, two layers, each masked by the glitter (the second offset by 117px, 71px) and by radial-gradient(at the light, rgb(0 0 0), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.3) 45%, rgb(0 0 0 / 0.12)):
    first: repeating-linear-gradient(60deg, rgb(255 139 210) 0 3%, transparent 5% 8%, rgb(139 243 255) 10% 13%, transparent 15% 18%, rgb(255 243 139) 20% 23%, transparent 25% 28%), size 260%, position (lx * 1.6, ly);
    second: repeating-linear-gradient(-35deg, rgb(169 139 255) 0 3%, transparent 5% 9%, rgb(139 255 196) 11% 14%, transparent 16% 20%, rgb(255 255 255) 22% 24%, transparent 26% 30%), size 260%, position (100% - lx, ly * 1.4).
    The dark gaps make each fleck light at its own angle and go out again.
  - Edge rgb(26 32 72). Glow hue 235.
- Chrome: a silver mirror whose highlights travel against the tilt.
  - Base: linear-gradient(125deg, rgb(228 230 234) 0%, rgb(141 147 158) 16%, rgb(246 247 249) 30%, rgb(124 130 141) 46%, rgb(217 220 225) 60%, rgb(148 154 165) 76%, rgb(241 242 244) 100%), background-size 220%, background-position (100% - lx, 100% - ly). Ink rgb(27 29 36).
  - Foil: linear-gradient(115deg, rgb(255 143 199), rgb(255 226 143) 14%, rgb(149 255 208) 28%, rgb(143 214 255) 42%, rgb(192 155 255) 56%, then again), size 240%, position at the light, overlay, opacity 0.3 + on * 0.35.
  - Glare: soft-light, white at 85%, 10% at 30%, black at 18% at 95%. Rim: base white at 18%, light white at 95%. An engraved look for printed lines: text-shadow 0 -1px 0 rgb(60 64 76 / 0.55), 0 1px 0 rgb(255 255 255 / 0.95).
  - Edge rgb(180 184 194). Glow hue 200.
- Etched: a pattern you only see in the light.
  - Base: matte rgb(18 18 20) with fine concentric rings, repeating-radial-gradient(circle at the artwork's center, rgb(255 255 255 / 0.05) 0 1.2px, transparent 1.6px 7px). Ink rgb(237 237 238).
  - Foil: linear-gradient(115deg, rgb(255 95 126), rgb(255 184 107) 10%, rgb(244 255 107) 20%, rgb(107 255 181) 30%, rgb(95 210 255) 40%, rgb(139 123 255) 50%, then again), size 300%, position at the light, masked by the same rings and by radial-gradient(at the light, rgb(0 0 0), rgb(0 0 0 / 0.5) 18%, transparent 42%); opacity 0.25 + on * 0.75. Glare opacity 0.2 + on * 0.4.
  - Keep the artwork window a plain matte panel (radial-gradient(70% 60% at 50% 35%, rgb(29 29 33), rgb(15 15 17))) so the rings stop at it.
  - Edge rgb(27 27 30). Glow hue 190.
- On every finish, the rim's base color is white at 5% unless listed, and its light color white at 50%. Text stays readable at every angle: check the lightest and darkest moment of the foil under it.

4. Turning over (only if chosen; Standard values)
- A click (or tap, or Enter and Space when focused) turns the card 180deg around its vertical axis on a spring (stiffness 70, damping 11), so it settles with a small overshoot in about 0.8s; the same again turns it back.
- It lifts toward the viewer while it turns: translateZ(|sin(angle)| * 40px); the shadow narrows by up to 45% and drops 14px at edge-on.
- Thickness 10px: the front sits 5px in front of the card's middle and the back 5px behind it, turned 180deg, both with backface-visibility hidden; between them, 10 copies of the card's outline in the finish's edge color, evenly spaced. Draw the edge only while turning.
- The back carries the same finish, glare and rim, with the light mirrored (lx becomes 100% - lx). Lay it out on the same margins as the front.
- Anything that changes the front (another finish, new content) changes while the card is edge-on, so it is never seen switching.

5. Depth inside the artwork (Standard values)
- Give each part of the artwork its own depth d behind the card's face (negative: in front of it), and move it by d * sin(angle): x = -d * sin(rotateY + turn), y = d * sin(rotateX). This is what real 3D would do.
- In the demo: the picture behind it 90px, the compass dial 50px, its middle ring 34px, the dashed ring 20px, the needle 12px in front (-12); the print in the corners sits on the surface and does not move. Draw the backmost layer larger than its window (100px on each side) so its edges never show.
- If the artwork can respond, let it: the compass needle springs toward the pointer (acceleration = 60 * angle difference - 5.5 * velocity, the short way round) and drifts by 12deg * sin(0.77t) + 6deg * sin(2.16t) when left alone; the dial turns 9deg a second and the dashed ring 18deg a second the other way. Small, slow, and one moving idea.

6. Rhythm and accessibility
- Hover in and out, tilt and light are continuous; the flip settles in about 0.8s.
- Switching finishes: cross-fade the faces over 420ms, or swap them while edge-on during a flip.
- Reduced motion: no tilt, no sway and no flip animation (the flip becomes an instant swap or a 200ms cross-fade); the light may still follow the pointer; the background stands still.
- The card keeps its role: a link or button stays one, the back is reachable by keyboard and announced, and nothing important is only visible at one angle.

7. The background (only if chosen)
- A glow behind the card: radial-gradient(closest-side, hsl(<finish's hue> 85% 64% / 0.3), transparent), 860px across, its opacity (0.04 + 0.12 * on) / 0.3.
- A slow fluid behind it: value noise in fBm (4 octaves, each turned by the matrix (1.6, 1.2; -1.2, 1.6), amplitude halving), warped twice: p = position / height * 1.25 + flow; q = (fbm(p), fbm(p + (5.2, 1.3) - flow.yx)); r = (fbm(p + 3.5q + (1.7, 9.2) + 1.3 * flow), fbm(p + 3.5q + (8.3, 2.8) - flow)); f = fbm(p + 3r). Color = mix(a, b, clamp(2.4f²)), then mix toward c by clamp(0.95 * |q| - 0.35), times 0.5 + 1.1f². Fade to the page color with smoothstep(0.82, 0.18, distance from (50%, 56%), y stretched 1.2). The flow moves round a circle of radius 0.33 about once every 40s; shift the field by (-rotateY, rotateX) * 0.008 so it answers the tilt.
- Palettes (a, b, c): Prism rgb(10 20 80), rgb(58 42 156), rgb(26 108 192); Rainbow rgb(44 12 64), rgb(12 68 80), rgb(90 32 52); Pearl rgb(51 40 94), rgb(28 74 74), rgb(92 44 80); Sparkle rgb(12 20 56), rgb(38 51 122), rgb(74 58 22); Chrome rgb(24 28 36), rgb(44 54 70), rgb(22 64 74); Etched rgb(13 15 18), rgb(26 36 40), rgb(38 42 50). Ease between palettes over about a second.
- Draw it at a third of its size, 30 times a second, and scale it up; it is soft, so nobody can tell.

8. How to build it, by platform
These are suggestions; check them against my stack and its versions, and choose what fits.
- Web (as in the demo): CSS 3D transforms with the layers as stacked elements and mix-blend-mode. Set the tilt as a transform on the card itself and the light as custom properties on the face only, never as inherited variables on a parent: changing a variable restyles everything under it. Move the glare as a 2x-sized layer with a transform, put the foil and the animated artwork on their own layers (will-change: transform), draw only the face that shows, and skip writes when a value has not changed. Drive everything from one requestAnimationFrame loop; the fluid is a small WebGL canvas.
- iOS (SwiftUI): rotation3DEffect with a perspective, the layers as overlays with .blendMode(.colorDodge / .overlay / .multiply), gradients positioned from the light, spring animations for tilt and flip; DragGesture for touch and CoreMotion (CMMotionManager deviceMotion) for phone tilt. A Metal [[stitchable]] colorEffect can draw the foil in one pass.
- Android (Compose): Modifier.graphicsLayer { rotationX; rotationY; cameraDistance = 12 * density }, Brush gradients drawn with BlendMode in drawWithContent, Animatable springs, pointerInput for drag, SensorManager (TYPE_GAME_ROTATION_VECTOR) for phone tilt. On API 33+, an AGSL RuntimeShader can draw the foil.
- Flutter: Transform with Matrix4.identity()..setEntry(3, 2, 0.0006)..rotateX()..rotateY(), the layers in a Stack with ShaderMask or CustomPainter blend modes, a FragmentProgram for the foil and the fluid, sensors_plus for phone tilt.
- Rust (wgpu, Bevy, egui): draw the card as one quad with a fragment shader that computes the foil, glare and rim from the light uniform, and transform it in 3D; the flip and edge are a second quad and a thin box.

9. Presets (around the Standard values; offer these when asking)
- Feel:
  Quiet: tilt 6deg, spring 120 / 18 (no visible overshoot), sway at half (about 1 to 1.5deg), hover strength capped at 0.7.
  Standard (recommended): tilt 12deg, spring 140 / 15, sway 2 to 3deg (section 1).
  Lively: tilt 16deg, spring 180 / 12 (a clear bounce), sway 3 to 4deg.
- Thickness: Thin 6px (6 layers), Standard 10px (10 layers, recommended), Thick 16px (16 layers); lift 30, 40 or 56px.
- Flip spring: Soft 55 / 9 (slower, more overshoot), Standard 70 / 11 (recommended), Crisp 110 / 18 (fast, no overshoot).
- Depth: None; Subtle (every depth halved); Standard (section 5, recommended).
- Pearl-like restraint for everyday products: Pearl with Quiet; Rainbow and Sparkle with Standard or Lively for moments worth celebrating.

10. Check
- Every finish at the four corners and in the middle: the text stays readable, the glare never washes out the print, the rim never reads as a solid line.
- Flip it many times quickly: it never shows both faces at once or a gap at the edge.
- The values built match the table I approved.
- It runs at the display's frame rate on a mid-range phone, and costs nothing when off screen; reduced motion and keyboard both work; light and dark pages both checked.

entries.summary: 用有限的字符密度，重建图像的明暗和轮廓。
entries.definition: 字符艺术用字形代替像素。把图像切成采样格，再根据每格亮度选择疏密不同的字符，就能保留轮廓。原帖第 003 期说明了字符采样，并提供可调参数。Kubai 另转引 @imperry 的首页动画作为应用案例。
entries.when: 实验性个人站、技术主题视觉，以及少量具有性格的装饰。
steps: 先选择清晰、明暗对比明确的素材。
用等宽字体并补偿字符格的宽高比例。
让画面保持装饰语义，提供文本说明与静态版本。
entries.avoid: 用字符图替代正文、持续刷新大面积 DOM，或让屏幕阅读器逐字朗读图案。
entries.prompt:
Add an ASCII / ordered-dither effect to one specific image or video in this project, with a live control panel next to it. Use the asset and the place I name (an , a , or a file path or URL, and the page or section it sits in); ask me if I have not named them. Apply the effect to that asset only, in place: keep its size, position, rounded corners and anything layered on top of it. If the project already has an image or canvas effect pipeline, or slider, segmented-control and panel components, build on them; otherwise create a reusable EffectLayer and EffectPanel.

Settings, one object shared by the layer and the panel: { filter: 'ascii' | 'dither', mask, palette, inkTone, strength, size, spacing } Keep separate values per filter, so switching filters brings back that filter's own settings.
What each control does in each filter, its range, and the recommended value (ASCII / Dither):

Mask effect, 0-100 (90 / 88): a vertical veil over the picture so the effect reads as texture rather than noise. Same in both filters.

Color, Original or one of five palettes (Original): gradient-maps the asset's luminance into one color family before filtering.
Sample tones, Shadows | Highlights (Shadows; ASCII only, hidden for Dither): which end of the tonal range becomes dense characters.
Sampling strength, 0-100 (100 / 100). ASCII: contrast of the tone curve and how bright and opaque the characters are. Dither: how few levels each color channel keeps (8 at 0, 2 at 100) and how fully the quantized color replaces the original.
Size, 0-100 (37 / 15). ASCII: font size, 7-24px. Dither: pixel block, 2-9px.
Spacing, 0-100 (0 / 0). ASCII: grid step, 8-24px across and 9-26px down, never tighter than the glyphs. Dither: scale of the Bayer pattern, 1-4 blocks per matrix cell.
Helpers used throughout:
range(v, a, b) = a + (b - a) * v / 100
luminance L = (0.299 R + 0.587 G + 0.114 B) / 255

s = strength / 100
"The box" is the asset's rendered size on the page.
Sampling:
Cover-fit the asset into the box and draw it into a small sampling canvas (about 480px on the long side), then read it with getImageData. A sample is the pixel under a point in the box, composited over white.
With a palette, recolor that canvas first: map each pixel's L through a 256-entry lookup built from the palette's four stops.

Per image or video frame, take about 12,000 evenly spaced samples: low = 8th percentile of L, high = 92nd percentile.
Shadows means dark ink, Highlights light ink.
ASCII:
Characters, from empty to full: " .,:;-=+xX08S#&@" (starts with two spaces).
Font: round(range(size, 7, 24))px monospace (22 instead of 24 when the box is under 720px wide), centered in each cell.

Grid: x step = max(range(spacing, 8, 24), widest glyph * 1.08); line height = max(range(spacing, 9, 26), height of "@" * 1.12, font * 1.04). The first cell sits half a step in from the edge.
Tone of a cell: raw = dark ink ? 1 - L : L; normalized = dark ink ? (high - L) / (high - low) : (L - low) / (high - low), clamped 0-1 (use raw alone when high - low < 0.025); mix = 0.72 + 0.14 s; t = raw (1 - mix) + normalized mix. Then a tone curve: black = 0.22 s, white = 1 - 0.08 s, lev = clamp((t - black) / (white - black), 0, 1), tone = lev (1 - s) + smoothstep(lev) s.
Skip cells with tone <= 0.02. Character = chars[round(tone * 16)]; skip spaces.
Ink: the sampled color lifted in HSV: value += (1 - value) * (0.24 + 0.18 s + 0.24 tone); saturation *= 1 + 0.16 + 0.2 s (clamped). Alpha = clamp((0.12 + 0.7 tone) (0.72 + 0.28 s), 0.06, 0.94).
Dither (ordered, Bayer 4x4):
pixel size = max(2, round(range(size, 2, 9))) (7 instead of 9 under 720px); pattern scale = max(1, round(range(spacing, 1, 4))); levels = max(2, round(range(strength, 8, 2))) per channel; blend = range(strength, 0.32, 1).
Matrix [[0,8,2,10],[12,4,14,6],[3,11,1,9],[15,7,13,5]]; threshold = (m + 0.5) / 16, indexed by floor(x / pattern scale), floor(y / pattern scale).

For each block sample its center, push saturation away from luma by 1 + 0.06 + 0.18 s, then per channel: scaled = c / 255 * (levels - 1); q = floor(scaled) + (fraction > threshold ? 1 : 0); out = c + (q / (levels - 1) * 255 - c) * blend.
Write the blocks into a canvas of box / pixel size and draw it scaled up with image smoothing off.
Mask and layering:
The mask is a vertical gradient with stops at the top, 42% and the bottom. Base opacities: on a light page white 54/20/38%, on a dark page black 44/20/50%. For a mask value v: stop = v <= 50 ? base * (v / 50)^1.08 : base + (100 - base) * ((v - 50) / 50)^1.08.
ASCII: draw the (recolored) picture, the mask, then the characters. Dither: draw the dithered picture, then the mask on top.

Changing filter or palette cross-fades from the last frame over 150ms.
Palettes (four stops at 0, 0.4, 0.74, 1):
meadow: #2B361F, #677D45, #AEBA78, #E5E1BD
blue: #192A4D, #326AC5, #A2C2F1, #EDF3FC
amber: #3C200F, #A74C15, #EF9A46, #F7E7CA
lavender: #292144, #6552AB, #B3A5E4, #F0ECFB

mono: #151515, #575757, #A6A6A6, #ECECEC
Rendering:
Draw into a canvas laid over the asset with the same size and corner radius, at devicePixelRatio capped at 1.6x and about 2048 x 2048.
Image: redraw when a setting changes (debounced 72ms).
Video: redraw on every new frame (requestVideoFrameCallback, falling back to requestAnimationFrame) while it plays and is on screen; keep the video element underneath as the source.
Control panel:

Place it next to the asset, below it when there is room, otherwise beside it, never covering it. About 420px wide, centered on the asset.
Rows, in order: Mask effect, Filter (two tabs: ASCII | Dither), Color (round swatches), Sample tones (ASCII only), Sampling strength, Size, Spacing (shown with %).
Each row 46px tall: a 136px label column, then the control. Slider: a 22px track with 8px radius and a filled part, a 9x30 rounded-rectangle thumb (3px radius), a number box with the value centered, and a snap mark at 50. Swatches: 22px circles, each filled with its palette's two middle stops at 135deg (Original: a tiny crop of the asset); the selected one gets a ring with a small gap.
Every change applies live while dragging. Add a "Reset to recommended" action that restores the values above for the current filter.

Follow the page's light or dark theme and the project's tokens.

entries.summary: 先建立一条共同的线，信息就有了可以依靠的骨架。

entries.definition: 字号体系把标题、正文、标签和辅助信息分配到有限的文字角色。层级由字号、字重、行高和空间共同建立，不能只靠把所有标题放大。本站将原帖的字号建议整理为实践步骤。
entries.when: 页面字号过多、标题与正文难区分，或辅助文字喧宾夺主时。
steps: 先列出文字的角色，再确定角色需要的视觉权重。
参考适合自己内容密度的成熟产品，建立少量可复用样式。
用真实中文、英文与长标题检查换行和行高。
entries.avoid: 机械照搬其他产品的像素数值，或通过过小、过淡的文字制造所谓高级感。
entries.prompt: 审查页面的文字角色，整理标题、正文、标签与辅助说明的字号、字重和行高。保留最小必要层级，以真实的中英文长内容检查可读性和换行。

entries.summary: 先给足以开始的信息，再让细节在需要时出现。
entries.definition: 渐进披露把低频细节放到后续层级，让当前任务保持清楚。本站从原帖关于说明文案的建议延伸这一概念：关键操作条件必须可见，补充背景则可以按需展开。
entries.when: 高级设置、补充说明和低频选项占据了主要任务区域时。
steps: 分清开始任务前必须知道的信息与补充背景。
把后者放到含义明确的展开入口中。
确保键盘与触屏都能打开，并保留展开后的阅读位置。

entries.prompt:
1. 使用组件化管理的思路处理 UI 组件，建立样式与色彩的变量体系，形成 Design Token，保证风格连续。

source.author: 枯白 Kubai

entries.summary: 拿起、经过、落下，每一步都告诉用户下一步会发生什么。
entries.definition: 可用的拖拽排序需要区分被拿起的对象、当前落点和附近对象的避让。动效表达空间关系，而排序结果仍然由明确的数据顺序控制。
entries.when: 任务排序、图标排列、播放队列和可自定义的列表。
steps: 拿起时强化当前对象，并显示明确的落点。
让附近对象用轻微位移预示排序结果。
提供按钮或键盘替代、取消操作，并播报最终顺序。
entries.avoid: 只支持鼠标拖动，或让排序动画改变命中区域，造成落点来回跳动。
entries.prompt:
Make drag-to-reorder in my product feel like this. Apply it to the lists,
rows and docks I name, and reuse any drag helper the project already has.

1. Cursor: a pointing hand over anything draggable, a grabbing hand while
   dragging.
2. Lift: the picked item follows the pointer, raised off the list so it
   never hides where it will land: above a horizontal row, or pulled aside
   and shrunk to about 90% in a vertical list. Its old slot closes up.
3. Drop hint: a faint, thin line in the gap where it will land (vertical in
   a row, horizontal in a list), about 15% of the text color. It grows from
   its middle when it appears and glides to each new gap. No line over the
   item's own slot.
4. Ripple: items on both sides of the line lean away from it. Counting n
   from the line (0 = the item touching it), item n moves
   A x 0.7^n (A is about 10px for icons, 8px for cards)
   and starts 24ms x n later, on a quick spring that barely overshoots and
   settles in about 0.25s. Nearer items move sooner and further, so the
   push spreads out like a ripple.
5. Drop: the item takes the gap and every item springs into its new place.
   Escape or dropping outside the list cancels, and everything springs back.
6. Give each motion its own curve (hand-like for the pointer, a small pop
   for the lift, springs for settling) instead of one ease-out everywhere.

Move things with transforms, not layout. Let the keyboard reorder too, and
with reduced motion keep only the line.

entries.when: 书籍、文档、作品集与具有真实预览内容的卡片。
steps: 把可点击区域固定在静止的外层。

entries.prompt:
Make the cards in my product open a little, like a book, when hovered.
At rest a card must look exactly as it does today; only hover or focus
reveals that it is a small book with pages inside.

## 0. Start from what exists
- Find the card component I name (or the one used in the grid or list I
  point to) and retrofit it in place. Reuse its markup, design tokens,
  radius, shadow and motion or spring utilities.
- Keep the card's footprint, padding, content and layout unchanged.
  Nothing around the card may move.
- If I ask for new cards instead, build a fresh square card (about
  280 x 280) in the style I choose below.
- Any option I leave unset uses the default marked *.

## 1. Choose a style
Default*: ordinary product cards, identical to normal ones until hovered.
- Surface: plain white (or my card surface token), no texture.
- Edge: a 1px hairline in my border colour.
- Shadow: light, neutral cool grey, half strength.
- Type: the product sans. Title 24/600, description 15 muted,
  meta 14 muted.
- Cover: the existing card UI: a 48px icon tile, a ↗ arrow top right,
  title, description, and a meta footer below a hairline.
- Wall: my normal page background.
- Pages: white, a faint shade toward the spine, a small heading and
  4-6 grey text lines.

Skeuomorphic: hardcover books on a gallery wall.
- Surface: fine bookcloth grain over a deep cover colour.
- Edge: a lit bevel: bright top edge, darker foot.
- Shadow: warm, near-neutral grey (never orange), full strength.
- Type: one serif title, bottom left. Nothing else on the cover.
- Cover: a full-bleed image or animated ASCII scene, with a soft gloss
  at the top and shade at the foot.
- Wall: warm plaster with a fine grain and a spotlight over each book.
- Pages: cream paper with grain, an italic chapter heading, justified
  lines, and thin page edges along the fore-edge.

Minimal: documentation volumes.
- Surface: flat off-white, light grey or graphite, one tone per card.
- Edge: a faint bevel or hairline.
- Shadow: cool neutral grey.
- Type: a mono section number and version on top, over a hairline rule;
  a two-line sans title and a small grey label at the foot.
- Cover: one small grey line diagram with a single element in the ink
  colour.
- Wall: cool grey with a faint 24px dot grid and soft light from above.
- Pages: cool white, a sans heading and grey lines.

Match my product: take surface, edge, shadow, type and wall from my
tokens, and keep the cover exactly as the card is today.

## 2. Options (defaults marked *)
- Intensity: subtle (A = 24deg) | book* (A = 42deg) | dramatic
  (A = 60deg).
- Pages: 2 | 3 | 4* | 6.
- Hinge: left* | right | top.
- Trigger: hover* | press (open while pressed) | scroll into view (open
  once when 60% visible, close after ~1.2s). Keyboard focus always
  opens it too.
- Pages show: blank paper | lines of text* | real preview content from
  the card (its next fields, a short list, a chart thumbnail).
- Cover: existing card UI* | image | animated ASCII scene | solid colour.
- Shadow direction: from above* | from top-left.
- Shadow strength: none | light | normal* | deep.
- Corners: match my tokens* | continuous (superellipse).
- Motion feel: snappy (k 320, damping 0.9) | default* (k 240,
  damping 0.86) | soft (k 160, damping 0.8). All barely overshoot.
- Reduced motion: tiny lift* | nothing.
- Touch: press* | scroll into view | off.

## 3. Layer stack
- Inside the card's link, put the cover on a body element with
  transform-style: preserve-3d. Behind it stack N pages and a back
  board, all absolutely positioned on the same square.
- Order, front to back: cover (n = 0), pages (n = 1..N), back board
  (n = N + 1, never moves).
- The cover keeps all of the card's existing content. Pages and the
  back board are decorative: aria-hidden, no links, no tab stops.
- Perspective on the static outer element: about 1100px, origin toward
  the hinge (30% 50% for left, 70% 50% for right, 50% 30% for top).
- transform-origin on the hinge edge of every layer: left 0 50%,
  right 100% 50%, top 50% 0. backface-visibility: hidden.
- Lift layer n by translateZ((N + 1 - n) x 0.6px) so layers never
  fight in depth.
- Pages sit 8px inside the cover (4px at the spine), like a book block,
  with radius = cover radius - 8.
- Back board: on flat cards (Default, Minimal) inset it ~6px from the
  cover with radius = cover radius - 6, so it never peeks out past the
  cover's foreshortened corners. On Skeuomorphic it is flush, the cover
  colour darkened ~28%.

## 4. Motion
- Layer n turns toward the viewer by
    angle(n) = A x 0.7^n
  and starts
    delay(n) = 28ms x n
  later. The cover leads; pages fan out behind it.
- Direction: rotateY(-angle) for a left hinge, rotateY(+angle) for
  right, rotateX(+angle) for top.
- Each layer runs on its own spring (see Motion feel), settling in
  about 0.3s.
- Close in reverse: the innermost page first, delay = 28ms x (N - n),
  back to 0deg.
- If the pointer leaves mid-way, retarget from the current angle and
  velocity. Never jump.
- No spring helper in the project? CSS transitions are fine: transition
  transform over ~420ms with a slight overshoot, e.g.
  cubic-bezier(0.3, 1.2, 0.5, 1), and set transition-delay to 28ms x n
  in the open state and 28ms x (N - n) at rest (the target state's delay
  applies, so closing runs in reverse).

## 5. Light and shading
- Light comes from above, so the shadow falls down the wall.
- The shadow is two solid shapes behind the card, each blurred once.
  At rest it hugs the card like any flat card's:
  - contact: small and darker, at the foot. Lower half of the card,
    ~4px in from each side, blur ~4px, ~2px down, ~22% opacity.
  - ambient: faint. Blur ~14px, ~6px down, ~12% opacity.
- Never a box-shadow: it is a hollow ring and shows as an outline once
  the cover swings off it.
- Tint: near-neutral grey nudged toward the wall (warm grey on a warm
  wall, cool grey on a cool one). Never pure black, never saturated.
- Strength scales both opacities: light 0.5 (Default style), normal 1,
  deep 1.4.
- Opening: crossfade to a second pre-blurred pair that is longer and
  softer (contact blur ~12px, 12px down; ambient blur ~38px, 26px down),
  and move it ~14px further down and ~4% wider with transform. Drive it
  with one progress value o (0..1) on its own spring (k 200, damping
  0.9): rest pair opacity 1 - o, open pair opacity o.
- Leaf shading: every page has an overlay gradient from the spine
  (32% dark -> 8% at 55% -> 0 at 85%). Its opacity is
    clamp(gap / 6, 0, 1) x max(0, 1 - gap / 30)
  where gap = the angle of the leaf in front minus this leaf's angle.
  A page is shaded while the leaf in front is just lifting off it, then
  lit once they part.
- Covers (Skeuomorphic, Minimal): a soft gloss at the top edge and a
  little shade at the foot.

## 6. Corners and edges
- Clip every layer (cover, pages, back board) to one shape path, and
  draw its edge (hairline or bevel) along that exact path, e.g. an SVG
  path stroked over the layer. Do not mix a CSS border or inset
  box-shadow with the clip: they disagree at the corners and show a
  second rim when the layers part.
- Match my tokens: use the token radius; nested radius = outer - inset.
- Continuous: superellipse corners |x|^n + |y|^n = 1 with n = 2^1.25
  (the same curve as CSS corner-shape: superellipse(1.25)). Generate a
  clip-path: path(...) per layer size, reuse it for the edge, and
  regenerate on resize.

## 7. Interaction and accessibility
- Hit-test on the resting footprint: listen for hover on the static
  outer element and give every moving layer pointer-events: none, so a
  swinging cover never moves the target and the card never flickers
  open and closed at its edges.
- Cursor: a pointing hand over the whole card.
- The whole card stays one <a> or <button> with its current accessible
  name. Pages add nothing to the accessibility tree.
- :focus-visible opens it exactly like hover. Keep the focus ring on the
  outer element, along the resting shape.
- Reduced motion: no fan and no rotation. The cover lifts ~2px and the
  shadow crossfades to the open pair.
- Touch: no hover. Use the Touch option; a tap must still activate the
  card on the first try.

## 8. Performance
- Animate transform and opacity only. Never animate blur, box-shadow,
  clip-path, width, height or top/left.
- Never animate a blur radius: blur each shadow once and crossfade the
  two pre-blurred versions.
- One requestAnimationFrame loop for all cards. Skip cards whose springs
  are at rest, and stop the loop when nothing moves.
- Write a style only when its value changes (cache the last string per
  element).
- No layout reads per frame: measure once, and again on resize
  (ResizeObserver).
- Animated canvas ∂∂: draw at ~30fps at most, and pause when off
  screen (IntersectionObserver) or when the tab is hidden.

## 9. Animated ASCII cover (only if chosen)
- Paint a small scene as one colour per character cell (~6 x 9px).
- Pick each character by brightness from " .:-=+*#%@".
- Draw a dimmed copy of the colours (~40%) underneath and the coloured
  characters on top, so the gaps read like a halftone.
- Stamp characters from a pre-rendered glyph atlas instead of laying out
  text every frame. Keep the motion slow and seamlessly looping.

## 10. When done
- List every file you changed or added.
- List the style and every option you used, marking which were
  defaults.
- Note anything that no longer looks identical at rest.

source.author: 枯白 Kubai

entries.summary: 用光影和按压状态，表现可以触碰的表面。
entries.definition: 按钮的实体感来自明暗、轮廓和按压反馈。原帖将同一语言应用到五种按钮层级，主要动作更突出，次要动作逐步减轻。
entries.when: 适合层级明确、希望建立触觉反馈的编辑器和播放器。
steps: 给主要操作保留最强对比。
统一上方光源，用顶边高光和底部接触阴影塑造体积。
按下时缩短阴影，并保留清晰的焦点边框。

entries.prompt:
Define a tactile, skeuomorphic Button component with five variants, from
strongest to weakest: primary, secondary, tertiary, ghost, text.
If the project already has a component library or design system, do not
add a new component: restyle its existing Button through its own variant
and token system, and keep its API, props and accessibility as they are.
Otherwise create one reusable Button with `variant` and `size` props.

Style: calm and precise, like the Lumno browser extension and the Cloudflare
dashboard. Neutral grays only, no brand hues. Lit from straight above.
No glossy Web 2.0 shine, no glow, no large blur.

Variants:
1. primary   - near-black slate face (#404859 -> #273042), white label
2. secondary - raised white key (#FFFFFF -> #F4F5F7), dark gray label
3. tertiary  - soft gray key (#F3F4F6 -> #E7E9EC), dark gray label
4. ghost     - no face at rest; faint gray fill on hover; a recessed well
               when pressed
5. text      - gray label with a thin underline and an arrow that nudges
               right on hover

Every filled variant is the same five material layers; only the values
change, so define them once as tokens and let each variant set its own:
1. Face: 180deg linear gradient, top 6-8% lighter than bottom.
2. Edge: 1px solid border one step darker than the bottom of the face
   (primary #12161F, secondary rgba(15,23,42,.14), tertiary rgba(15,23,42,.1)).
3. Top highlight: inset 0 1px 0 white (18% on slate, 85-100% on light
   faces). Put every inset layer in the button's own box-shadow, before the
   drop layers, never on a pseudo-element overlay: inset shadows on the
   element follow the inner radius (outer radius minus border), so the
   corners line up in every state.
4. Bottom shade: inset 0 -1px 0 black (22% on slate, 6% on light faces).
5. Drop shadow in two layers: a tight contact shadow 0 1px 2px plus a soft
   lift 0 4px 10px -3px (18% and 28% on slate, about a third of that on
   light faces).

States (hover, pressed/active, focus-visible, disabled):
- Hover: face one step lighter; the lift grows to 0 8px 16px -5px.
- Pressed: translateY(1px); flip the gradient (darker on top); the outer
  shadow collapses to 0 1px 1px; the top highlight becomes an inner shadow,
  inset 0 1px 2px black (40% on slate, 12-16% on light faces). Light faces
  keep a 1px white line below, 0 1px 0 rgba(255,255,255,.9), like a key
  pressed into paper.
- Give rest and pressed the same number of inset layers (pad with
  inset 0 0 0 transparent) so the shadow animates instead of jumping.
- Focus-visible and disabled follow the library's existing conventions.
- Timing: 120ms for transform, 140ms for shadows, 160ms for colors.

Sizes: all values above are for the 14px label size: height 40px,
padding 0 18px, radius 10px, label weight 600, optional 16px leading icon.
On the slate face add a label text-shadow 0 -1px 0 rgba(0,0,0,.28).
Scale the material with the type, never keep it at fixed pixels: express
every length (height, padding, radius, border, icon, the 1px press offset,
and every shadow offset, blur and spread) as a multiple of a size unit
u = label size / 14. Provide two sizes: md (14px label, u = 1px) and
lg (16px label, u = 16/14 px, so height 45.7px, radius 11.4px, lift shadow
0 4.6px 11.4px -3.4px).

entries.when: 适合使用鼠标的桌面级联菜单。
steps: 判断指针是否进入朝向子菜单的区域。
只在该区域内短暂延迟切换。
键盘用方向键进入与返回，触屏通过点击展开。
