entries.summary: 让卡片跟随滚动位置，展开、叠放或切换焦点。
entries.definition: 原帖展示层叠、飞出、横向展廊、封面轮播和图片展开。共同点是滚动进度直接决定画面，暂停时停在当前状态，反向时顺应回退。
entries.when: 适合产品功能演示或作品集中的短章节。
steps: 先让内容按自然顺序可读。
挑一种能解释内容关系的运动。
给触屏、键盘和减少动态模式保留完整内容。
entries.avoid: 劫持整页滚动或将重要信息放在必须操作特效才能到达的位置。
entries.prompt:
Rework a long page that already exists in my product so its cards move with scrolling. This changes my product, not a new page or a demo: keep my content, components, tokens and copy, find the sections that deserve it, and give each one of five scroll-driven card interactions: stacked cards (each new card covers the last, which shrinks and dims), a card deck (the top card flies off to one side and the next rises), a pinned gallery (the section holds still while scrolling moves a row sideways), a cover flow (the middle cover is largest; the others shrink, turn away and dim), or an image expand (a picture grows from a frame to the whole screen, with words behind and in front of it rising at different speeds for depth). The scroll position drives every effect, so the reader sets the pace and scrolling back plays it in reverse. It must hold up on every screen, phones above all, and at every viewport height (section 8).

Every value here is a recommendation. Sections 2 to 8 are a tested set (Standard); section 10 gives presets. I choose; you build what I choose.

First look at my product (section 0). Then ask me these one at a time, each as a short list of options with key values and the recommended one marked, and wait for my answer:
1. Which sections get which interaction (section 1): at most one of each per page, with ordinary sections between them.
2. Length: Short, Standard (recommended) or Long (section 10).
3. Phones and short screens: Standard (recommended: on phones the stack, deck and image expand stay, sized to the viewport; the gallery and cover flow become native horizontal rows with snap points; below 560px of viewport height nothing pins), the same as desktop, or plain sections on all phones. Tell me which screen sizes my analytics or audience suggest, if you can find out.
4. Reduced motion: plain sections (recommended: lists, horizontal rows, a full-width picture), or keep the pinning and drop the motion.
5. Engine: CSS scroll-driven animations with a small script as fallback (recommended), or the scroll library my project already uses. Never smooth-scrolling or scroll-hijacking.
Then sum up my choices in one table, propose how you will build it on my platform (section 9), with cost and fallback, and wait for my go-ahead.

0. Start from what exists
- The page: its sections in order, their content, cards, images and videos, and anything fixed or sticky (header, banner, cookie bar) with its height per breakpoint.
- For each section, which interaction fits and which sections must stay as they are (anything people scan, compare or search).
- How the layout responds today: breakpoints, how it sizes to the viewport (vh, svh, dvh, JS reading innerHeight), what already breaks on short screens.
- How the page scrolls: window or inner container, smooth-scroll libraries, anchor links, existing scroll effects.
- Platform and versions, tokens for radius and motion, dark mode. Tell me in a few lines before asking.

1. Which interaction for which content
- Stacked cards: 3 to 5 parallel items worth a screen each (steps, features, plans, chapters).
- Card deck: 3 to 6 items seen one at a time (picks, testimonials, highlights).
- Pinned gallery: 5 to 12 items wider than the screen, to browse (work, products, releases).
- Cover flow: 5 to 9 items of the same shape, one in focus (albums, books, plans, people).
- Image expand: one strong picture or video that opens the next chapter.

2. The rule behind all five
- Each section has one progress p = clamp((scrollY - start) / distance, 0, 1), and every property is a function of p, never a timed animation that scroll merely starts. Stopping halfway leaves it halfway; scrolling back reverses it exactly. Never change scroll speed, snap or catch the wheel.
- Pinning is position: sticky inside a section taller than the screen; the extra height is the distance the effect plays over.
- Animate only transform, opacity, clip-path and filter. Text stays in the page and readable at every p.
- When a section is pinned, show where the reader is as quietly as possible: a thin bar or dots, never a label.

3. Stacked cards (demo: 1000 x 896 viewport)
- Cards 936 x 720 (all 12 columns, bled 24px so their 24px padding puts content back on the columns), corners 28px, 48px apart.
- Each sticks 16px lower than the last: top = 40px + i * 16px (add a fixed header's height). Newer cards cover older ones, leaving a 16px strip of each.
- A card recedes as later ones arrive: k = clamp((scrollY - when it stuck) / 752px, 0, cards after it); scale = 1 - k * 0.05 from its top center (0.85 under three), dark layer at k * 0.12.
- Inside a card, the name and one line sit on columns 0 to 5 and wrap there, never into the picture; the name starts 48px below the card's top, the line 24px under it.
- Give each card its own muted tint and picture (demo: stone, sage, clay, then one ink card). No shadows.
- After the last card sticks, hold 320px, then the stack leaves together.
- Optional opening: the section's title sized to span the grid exactly (not cropped), the first card covering its foot; it moves at half the scroll and fades out over the 280px before the first card sticks.

4. Card deck
- Five cards in a pile, 432 x 456 (six columns, centred) under the title; each holds a picture 8px in, then a name and one line 24px in, nothing else.
- Section 100vh + 1920px, pinned: 420px of scrolling throws each of the first four cards, then a 240px hold. The last card stays.
- Card i: t = clamp((scrollY - start) / 420 - i, 0, 1). It flies to one side, alternating: x = side * t * t * 1000px, y = t * (160px * t - 40px), rotate = side * t * 16deg about its bottom center. Hidden once thrown; scrolling back returns it on the same path.
- Cards below sit 18px lower and 0.05 smaller per place, dark layer 0.04 per place, at most three deep, rising a place as the top card goes.

5. Pinned gallery
- 5 to 12 cards in a row: demo eight, 280 wide (four columns) and 24px apart, each a white card with its picture 8px in, then name and artist. Title above, 48px clear of the row; a 2px bar below (track 6% black, fill 30%).
- Section 100vh + overflow (row width minus viewport width, 1520px in the demo); content sticky at top 0, 100vh tall.
- p = (scrollY - start) / overflow; the row moves translateX(-p * overflow), no easing: scrolling turned sideways. It lets go at the last item.
- Keep the pinned distance under about three screens; more items belong in a grid.

6. Cover flow
- 5 to 9 square covers, 432 (six columns, centred), under the title, dots below, no text on the covers.
- Section 100vh + 320px per step, pinned. r = clamp((scrollY - start) / 320, 0, count - 1); c = floor(r) + smoothstep(fract(r)), so each cover rests in the middle a moment.
- For cover i, d = i - c: translateX = d * 260px, rotateY = clamp(d, -1, 1) * -30deg, scale = max(0.6, 1 - |d| * 0.2), dark layer min(|d|, 3) * 0.15, nearest on top. Perspective 1400px. Hide beyond 3.5 places. Dots light by 1 - |i - c|.

7. Image expand
- Section 100vh + 1200px, pinned: 900px to grow, 300px to hold.
- At the start the title and a 584 x 352 frame (columns 2 to 9, 48px below it) are centred together, corners 8px.
- The picture always covers the viewport; clip-path: inset() shows the frame and opens to 0 with no corners, while the picture settles from scale 1.2 to 1, so it reads as growing. Both on e = ease(p), cubic-bezier(0.45, 0, 0.25, 1). The title fades at twice the speed and rises 60px.
- Depth: cut the main shape out of the picture as its own layer (demo: the hills), set a title behind it with its foot hidden by the shape, and one small line in front. As it opens, each settles from its own scale (picture and shape 1.2, title 1.25, line 1.4). Once full, the picture and shape stay still while the title rises at 0.25 of the scroll and the line at 0.5. Something behind something, moving at another speed, reads as perspective.
- Then the next section slides over it with 28px top corners that flatten over its last 120px, while the picture darkens to 35% black. A video works the same, muted and looping, only while on screen.

8. Screens and viewport heights
The demo's sizes are for a 1000 x 896 viewport. Scale them to the screen; never a fixed height that assumes a tall window.
- Size pinned sections with 100svh, not 100vh: on phones 100vh is the height with the toolbar hidden, so content runs under the toolbar. Never dvh for pinned content; it jumps as the toolbar moves.
- Measure on load, on orientation change and when the width changes. Ignore height-only resizes under about 120px (the toolbar showing and hiding); recomputing then makes cards jump mid-scroll.
- Fit each pinned section into one screen:
  - Stacked card height = min(720px, 100svh - sticky top - (cards - 1) * 16px - 32px); the distance between cards sticking follows it.
  - Deck: title + 48px + card fit in 100svh - 64px; the picture gives up height first.
  - Gallery card height = min(520px, 100svh - title - 48px - 96px).
  - Cover size = min(432px, 48svh, 70vw); the spread scales with it.
  - Image frame = min(584px, 100vw - 2 * margin) wide at 5:3; the insets follow from it.
- Scale every scroll distance by clamp(0.7, viewport height / 896, 1.2).
- Below 560px of height (a phone in landscape, a short window), nothing pins: lists, horizontal rows, a full-width picture.
- Type follows the width: section titles clamp(36px, 7vw, 64px), card names clamp(28px, 5vw, 36px).
- Full-bleed moments respect env(safe-area-inset-*). Subtract a fixed header from every fit and sticky top.

Layout and type (all sections)
- Lay everything on the column grid first. Every text box is as wide as its columns, so long names wrap instead of running into a picture.
- What a title introduces starts 48px below it; in a pinned section the title and content are centred in the viewport together; centred titles over centred content, left-aligned over left content.
- Keep the cards in focus: outside them one short title per section, no tags, side copy, counters or captions; inside them one structure: picture, name, one line.
- Two typefaces in four sizes (demo: Newsreader 64 and 36, Geist 18 and 16). Pull large serif lines left by their first letter's side bearing; above about 100px use a text optical size so serifs stay blunt.
- No dividers except between list rows, no drop shadows, the accent colour once at most. One picture style per group, and never the same picture twice on a page.
- Anchor links land at a section's start. Keyboard scrolling works like the wheel; items in pinned sections stay reachable with Tab.

Check
- Each section slow, fast and backwards: no jumps, flicker or gaps.
- Viewports 375x667, 390x844, 430x932 (toolbar shown and hidden), 844x390, 768x1024, 1280x720, 1440x900, 1920x1080, and a 600px-tall desktop window: nothing cut off, no card taller than the screen, nothing under a toolbar or fixed header.
- 200% text zoom, reduced motion, keyboard, light and dark; full frame rate on a mid-range phone; the values built match my table.

9. How to build it
Check these against my stack and versions.
- Web: position: sticky for pinning; scroll-driven animations (animation-timeline: view() or a named timeline, animation-range). Where unsupported, or where keyframes are not enough (the deck's per-card ranges, the cover flow's resting steps), one passive scroll listener reads scrollY once per frame, computes each section's p from offsets measured on resize, and writes it as a custom property on that section only.
- If the project already uses GSAP ScrollTrigger (scrub, pin) or Motion (useScroll, useTransform), use it with these values; never add one only for this.
- iOS (SwiftUI): .scrollTransition or .visualEffect on the view's frame in the scroll view (onScrollGeometryChange on iOS 18), scaleEffect, rotation3DEffect, offset, clipShape; gallery and cover flow as horizontal ScrollViews with .scrollTargetBehavior(.viewAligned).
- Android (Compose): LazyListState for p, Modifier.graphicsLayer for scale, rotationY, alpha, translation and clip; LazyRow with snapping or HorizontalPager.
- Flutter: CustomScrollView with slivers, a ScrollController for p, Transform and ClipRRect; PageView for gallery and cover flow.

10. Presets
- Length: Short (stack 560px, deck 300px, gallery 1.25px sideways per 1px, cover step 240px, picture 600 + 200px), Standard (752, 420, 1:1, 320, 900 + 300, recommended), Long (900, 560, 1:1 with 200px held at each end, 420, 1200 + 400).
- Stack depth: Flat (scale 0.03, shade 0.08 per card), Standard (0.05, 0.12), Deep (0.07, 0.16, 24px strips).
- Deck throw: Gentle (8deg, 700px, always right), Standard (16deg, 1000px, alternating), Lively (24deg, 1200px, 60px lift).
- Cover flow: Flat (no turn, sides at 0.85), Standard (30deg, 0.8), Deep (45deg, 0.75, 180px apart).
- Picture start: Small (420 x 280), Standard (584 x 352), Wide band (full width, 340 tall).

entries.prompt:
# Small animations for a product site's feature tiles

Give every tile in my site's feature grid a small animation: a tiny scene that shows what the feature does.

## 0. Before you build
- Read the project: find out the tech stack (plain HTML/CSS, React, Vue, Svelte, Astro, Tailwind, Framer Motion…) and build it the way the project already does. Don't add an animation library unless the project already uses one.
- Ask me which look to use:
  A. The Lumno material below, as written.
  B. My product's own style: take the colors, radii, borders and shadows from my existing design tokens and components, and keep only the structure and motion rules from this prompt.
  C. A mix: the Lumno material in my brand's accent color and radii.
- Picking features: if I named features, animate those. If not, read the product's site, docs or code, list 3–5 features that a short scene can explain, and let me pick.

## 1. Lumno material (option A)
Overall: quiet, neutral, precise. Hairlines instead of borders, soft shadows tinted warm, no gradients or color washes, one accent color.

- Grid: one card with an outer radius of 28px. Cells are separated by 1px hairlines (a 1px grid gap over a hairline color). Cells are white. The card has a faint hairline ring and a soft shadow.
- Art panel: inset 8px from the cell edge, with a radius of the card radius minus the inset (20px), so corners stay concentric.
  - Fill #fafafa, plus an inner 1px ring: box-shadow: inset 0 0 0 1px rgba(32,38,46,.07).
  - Texture: background: repeating-linear-gradient(-45deg, rgba(32,38,46,.06) 0 1px, transparent 1px 7px).
  - The scene sits centred on the panel, about 126×118px.
- Text bars: body bars 4px tall with a 2px radius in #e5e9ef; heading bars 5px tall in #cdd4de. Vary the widths (34–92px).
- Mini windows and cards: white with a 9px radius.
  - Shadow: 0 0 0 1px rgba(47,42,34,.06), 0 8px 20px -10px rgba(47,42,34,.25).
  - Tab strip: 20px tall, #eef1f5. Tabs: 16px tall with 6px top corners; the active tab is white.
  - Favicons: 10px.
- Inner surfaces such as charts or fields: #f4f6fa. Secondary data: #b9c9e0. Accent: #3462ad, used only on the result.
- Icon chip (top-left of each tile): 32px, 10px radius, 1px border rgba(32,38,46,.1), white, shadow 0 1px 2px rgba(32,38,46,.05), a line-style glyph in #4b5563.
- Text color: a warm near-black, #2f2a22.
- Hover: the cell darkens to about 2.5% grey; the panel goes to #f4f5f6 with its ring at .09; the icon chip grows 32→36px from its top-left corner, its glyph turns to the text color, and its shadow deepens slightly.
- Dark mode (suggested values; keep the same relationships):
  - Cells #17181a, panel #1d1f22, inner ring rgba(255,255,255,.06), texture rgba(255,255,255,.04).
  - Body bars #2c2f34, heading bars #3a3e45.
  - Windows #24272b with a 1px rgba(255,255,255,.06) outline and a shadow of 0 8px 20px -10px rgba(0,0,0,.6).
  - Tab strip #1a1c1f, accent #6f9bea, text #ecebe8.

## 2. Scene
- One idea per tile: 2–4 moves that show "action → result", such as "click → a small window opens" or "change here → the other side syncs".
- Abstract wireframes only: no screenshots and no real text. Use at most one small icon where something needs to be recognisable.
- Motion: ease-out for movement, cubic-bezier(.22,1,.36,1); a slight spring for appearing, cubic-bezier(.34,1.4,.64,1). Each move takes 250–600ms; the whole scene is done in about 3s.
- Icon chip: when the tile plays, its glyph redraws stroke by stroke (draw, pop or slide per part), then hands back to the solid icon.

## 3. Playback
- Resting styles are the final frame. Animations only describe where things come from (fill-mode: both or equivalent), so reduced motion shows the result and an interrupted play never jumps.
- The art panel fades in (opacity, plus translateY 6px and scale .97 to none) as its tile first plays.
- Play once in view: when about 70% of the tile is visible, wait ~200ms, then play. Tiles that enter together go ~250ms apart, in reading order. Stop on the final frame.
- One "played" state (a class or data attribute) drives every animation in the tile. To replay: remove it, force a reflow, add it back (or re-key in a framework).
- On mouse hover (mouse only) or keyboard focus, replay: blur the final frame out over ~160ms (blur 6px, opacity 0), restart under the blur, then clear it. Don't restart a play that hasn't finished.
- Optional loop on hover: while the pointer stays on the tile, replay again ~600ms after each play ends. When the pointer leaves, finish the current play and rest on the final frame.
- Touch: a tap follows the tile's link; nothing depends on hover.
- prefers-reduced-motion: reduce: no animation; show the final frame.

## 4. Colors and dark mode
- Every color is a variable on the art panel (panel, ring, texture, bars, windows, tab strip, accent, shadow); no hard-coded colors in the rules.
- Follow prefers-color-scheme, and the project's manual theme switch too (a class or data-theme), if it has one.
- Check it in both light and dark.

## 5. Delivery
- Mark the art as decorative (aria-hidden) and keep translatable text out of it.
- Check it in a real browser: first play, hover replay, keyboard focus, reduced motion, dark mode and a phone-width layout.

entries.when: 审查设置页、填写后统一提交的表单，以及工具栏里的下拉入口时。
steps: 写下每个选择何时生效。独立且即时的开关项用 Switch，随表单保存的多选项用复选框。
区分值和动作。选语言后字段显示当前语言；选菜单里的「导出」则启动导出，入口名称保持原样。
比较选项数和长度。两到五个简短互斥项可平铺为分段选择；选项多或文字长时用下拉选择，必要时加入搜索和空状态。
需要同时展示所有候选项时，单选用 Radio，多选用复选框。若允许暂不决定，为单选题提供明确选项。
entries.avoid: 把「开」和「关」做成两枚单选按钮，或让本应随表单保存的选择悄悄立即生效。
entries.prompt:
Review the choice controls in my product (switches, checkboxes, radio buttons, segmented controls, selects and dropdown menus) and decide for each one whether it is the right control. Diagnose first; change only what I approve, in my own code and components, without new dependencies.

1. Read the product
Find every place a person picks something, turns something on or off, or runs an action from a list. For each, note what it sets or does, how many options it has, how many can be picked, and whether it takes effect at once or on Save.

2. How to choose
a. Switch or checkbox: when it takes effect.
- Switch: takes effect the moment it is flipped (settings that save on their own, no Save button).
- Checkbox: one answer in a form, applied on Submit or Save.
- One thing on or off is one switch, never two radios (On / Off). If both sides have names of their own (Light / Dark), it is a choice of one: see (c).

b. Select or dropdown menu: a value or an action.
- Select: holds a value; after a pick the field shows it, and the picked option has a tick in the list.
- Dropdown menu: holds actions (Export, Duplicate, Delete). A pick runs it, the button keeps its name, and the result shows elsewhere. Menus go in page headers, toolbars and row ends, not among form fields. A split button pairs a main action with a menu of related ones (Send, with Send later and Save as draft beside it).
- Tabs switch to other content and set nothing; a segmented control sets a value or the view of the same content.

c. One of several: by the number of options.
- 2 to 5 short options: a segmented control.
- 2 to 5 that each need a line: radio buttons, stacked under the label.
- 6 or more, or labels that change or grow (names, dates, items people add): a select, so the layout never shifts.
- Hundreds (time zones, countries, people): a select with search, and a clear message when nothing matches.

d. Radio or checkbox: how many can be picked.
- Radio: exactly one, all options in view, as in a survey question. It can't be cleared once picked, so add a "none" option (Not sure yet) when that is a fair answer.
- Checkbox: any number, none included.
- Inside a select: a tick for one value, never radio circles; a checkbox before each option for several, with the picks shown as chips in the field.

3. Report before changing
Give me a table, one row per control: where, what it sets or does, the control now, the control it should be (or "right as it is"), why in one line, and anything else that changes (a Save button, a "none" option, an action moved out of a form). Flag every change in behaviour, ask about cases that could go either way, and wait for me to choose.

4. Change what I approve
Use my components, or the platform's own controls when I have none. Keep the values people already saved. Check that switches act at once and checkboxes on submit, selects show their value, menu buttons keep their name, and everything works by keyboard and screen reader.

entries.summary: 沿弧线排列卡片，连续改变曲率，让视角从环内过渡到环外。
entries.definition: 在 Kubai 的示例中，环内视角让两侧的卡更靠近观看者。转到环外时，正中的卡最清晰，两侧和后排逐渐失焦。两种视角共用同一条弧线，观看者可以跟住同一张卡。
entries.when: 在作品集或图片浏览器里同时展示一组有前后关系的画面时。
steps: 先用纯色卡片检查弧度和遮挡顺序。在环内视角下，两侧的卡应比中间的更大。
连续改变曲率切到环外，观察中心卡是否保持清晰，再给远处的卡加景深。
最后加上渐变和翻面。从中间向两边依次翻开，检查背面图片的方向。
entries.avoid: 用模糊掩盖卡片错位。先关闭景深检查几何关系，再恢复材质。
entries.prompt:
Build a ring of cards in my project, in two views. Inside: the viewer stands in the middle of the ring, the cards near the edges come closer and grow, and they pass under a rim of glass at each side of the frame that bends them and splits their colors. Outside: the ring is seen at eye level from outside, the front card is in focus, the sides and the far side soften with distance, and switching to it turns the cards over, one after another, from flowing gradients to pictures. Every card's gradient flows slowly. A settings panel shows the key numbers as sliders, set to the defaults below, so they can be tuned live.

Every value here comes from a working demo and is the default, not a requirement. Build it with these values first, then let me tune them with the panel (section 8).

Before building, look at my project (section 0) and ask me these, one at a time, with the recommended answer marked:
1. Where it goes: its own page or section (recommended), or a component I name.
2. What the cards hold: flowing gradients on the front and my pictures on the back (recommended; tell me where the pictures come from), gradients only, or pictures only (then skip the turn-over and show the pictures in both views).
3. The view it opens in: Inside (recommended) or Outside, and whether people can switch (a two-option segmented control, recommended).
4. The settings panel: shown to everyone, shown only in development, or hidden behind a toggle.
Then sum up my answers, say how you will build it on my platform (section 9), and wait for my go-ahead.

0. Start from what exists
- Find how the project draws (DOM, canvas or WebGL, a native view tree, a GPU renderer), its framework and versions, where the pictures live, its slider or form components, and whether it has a dark mode and a reduced-motion setting.
- Tell me in a few lines what you found before asking.

1. The ring
- N cards of w x h, a gap between them, one step = w + gap apart along an arc. Default: N = 22, 180 x 300, gap 18, so step 198 and radius R = N * step / (2 * PI) ≈ 693. The ring's circumference is exactly the row, so it closes on itself.
- Each card i sits at s = wrap(i * step - offset) along the arc, wrapped into [-N * step / 2, N * step / 2). offset is how far the row has moved; the front card is round(offset / step) mod N.
- One signed curvature c = bend / R places every card: for c = 0, x = s, z = 0, a = 0; otherwise a = s * c, x = sin(a) / c, z = (1 - cos(a)) / c. x runs across, z toward the viewer, and the card turns by a about its upright middle. bend = 1 is Inside (the ring curves toward the viewer), bend = -1 is Outside.
- Switching views eases bend from one to the other over 1100ms with cubic-bezier(0.65, 0, 0.35, 1), so the row visibly bends from one ring into the other.

2. The camera
- Perspective P is the eye's distance from the front card: P = mix(pIn, pOut, (1 - bend) / 2), so it moves with the switch. Defaults: pIn 860 (a little behind the ring's center, so the row curves without pulling the side cards too far; at P = R the eye is exactly at the center), pOut 1500 (well back, so the ring turns away gently).
- The eye looks straight on, at the cards' middle height. A point (x, y, z) lands on screen at x * P / (P - z), y * P / (P - z), from the frame's center.
- Leave out a card when any part of it is less than 140 units in front of the eye, or when it is wholly off the frame.
- Inside, the 22-card ring at pIn 860 shows five cards: three whole, the outer two going into the glass. Outside it shows the whole ring, the far side between and beyond the near cards.

3. The card face
- Corners: a continuous curve, a superellipse of exponent 4 over a 32px radius, the same curve as CSS corner-shape: superellipse(2). In a shader, the distance to the outline is: d = abs(p) - (w, h) / 2 + r; m = max(d, 0); dist = (m.x^4 + m.y^4)^(1/4) + min(max(d.x, d.y), 0) - r.
- Front: a flowing gradient of four colors (section 4). Back: a picture, shown mirrored so it reads the right way round when the card is turned.
- No shadow, no reflection, no darkening as cards turn away: on a white page they only look dirty. Depth comes from size, blur and fade (section 6).
- Pressing a card shrinks it to 0.95 in 140ms and back in 320ms, about its middle.

4. The fluid gradient
- Value noise in fBm, 3 octaves; after each octave turn the point by the matrix (0.8, -0.6; 0.6, 0.8), scale it by 2.02, add (1.7, 9.2), and halve the amplitude.
- With p the point on the card in pixels from its middle: uv = p / w * 0.9 + seed (seed = i * 3.7 + 0.43, so every card differs).
- The flow moves the field around a circle: o1 = rho * (cos(phi), sin(phi)), o2 = rho * (cos(phi + 2.1), sin(phi + 2.1)). phi grows with time so the field moves 0.2 noise cells a second (the Flow slider, 20%); rho is the circle's radius. Because the field comes back to where it began, a recording or a loop never jumps. In the demo one turn takes the length of the animation loop (17.07s).
- Warp it twice: w1 = (fbm(uv + o1), fbm(uv + (5.2, 1.3) - o1)); w2 = (fbm(uv + 1.5 * w1 + (1.7, 9.2) + o2), fbm(uv + 1.5 * w1 + (8.3, 2.8) - o2)); f = fbm(uv * 0.9 + 1.7 * w2).
- Color: mix(c0, c1, smoothstep(0.3, 0.7, f)), then toward c2 by smoothstep(0.42, 0.72, w2.x) * 0.9, then toward c3 by smoothstep(0.5, 0.8, w1.y) * 0.7; a soft light across the top (toward white by smoothstep(0.1, -0.6, y / h) * 0.12); film grain of ±1.75% that fades out under blur.
- Palettes, four colors each, one per card, for example: Tangerine #ff7a3d #ff3d77 #ffc46b #7a2cff; Lagoon #00c2c7 #2f6bff #9ff3e0 #0b2a6f; Peony #ff8fb1 #ffd1dc #b84dff #ff5a5f; Citrus #ffe14d #7ee081 #ff9f1c #2ec4b6; Iris #6a5cff #b18cff #ff7ad9 #1b1464; Aurora #2af598 #009efd #b3ffab #12123a. Or derive them from my brand colors and show me.

5. Inside: the glass rim
- Draw the cards into a texture first, then lay it on screen in a second pass. Along each side of the frame is a band of glass, rim = 160px wide.
- A pixel at distance d from its side (d < rim) shows the picture from further in: k = (1 - d / rim)^2.4, and the offset is 0.4 * rim * k across, toward the middle, along the line toward the eye point (so it also moves toward the eye's height). The cards' top and bottom edges flare out under the glass, and the flare grows smoothly from nothing at the band's inner side.
- Keep 0.4 * 2.4 under 1: the band then squeezes the picture toward the edge but never folds it back on itself. A fold repeats a card, or a gap between cards, inside the glass.
- Dispersion: take the offset at seven strengths, red bending furthest and blue least: for t = i / 6, i = 0..6, the offset times 1 + spread * (1 - 2t), with spread = 0.25 * k (the Dispersion slider, 25%). Weight each sample by w(t) = clamp((1.5 - 3t, 1 - 1.5 * |2t - 1|, 3t - 1.5), 0, 1) and divide by the summed weights, so the fringe runs smoothly through the colors.
- A faint light along the glass: toward white by k^3 * 0.12.
- The rim belongs to Inside only: it fades out as bend goes to 0, and a 0 rim switches it off.

6. Outside: depth of field
- Blur b, in screen pixels, is the larger of two: across the frame, blur * smoothstep(110, half the frame's width, |screen x|)^1.4, so the middle 220px stays sharp and the blur grows smoothly toward the sides; and with distance, blur * smoothstep(0.25, 0.8, back)^1.2, where back = -z / (2R) goes from 0 at the front card to 1 at the far side. Default blur 14px.
- Work the blur out per pixel, never with a backdrop blur over moving content (it shimmers). For a card, take its coverage as a box blur in screen pixels, separately across and up: across = clamp((min(dl, b) + min(dr, b)) / (2b), 0, 1), where dl and dr are the screen distances to the card's left and right sides; the same for up and down; alpha = smoothstep(across) * smoothstep(down), capped by the corners softened by the same b. A card narrower than the blur never reaches full cover and fades, as a real blur would.
- Draw each card with a margin of (the largest blur + 4) screen pixels around it, so a blurred edge always has room, however steeply the card is turned.
- Blur the content too: fade out the noise octaves finer than the blur, and read the pictures from a smaller mipmap level, log2(max(1, b * texels per screen pixel)).
- The far side fades toward the page: toward white by fade * smoothstep(0.3, 1, back). Default fade 50%.

7. Turning over, and motion
- Switching to Outside turns every card over about its upright middle, one after another from the front card out: for the whole run flip going 0 to 1 over 1800ms with cubic-bezier(0.3, 0, 0.6, 1), each card's lag = min(|s| / (6 * step), 1) and its turn = PI * smoothstep(0, 1, flip * 1.55 - lag * 0.55). The front half ends showing pictures and the far half its gradients. Switching back turns them back.
- Drag: the row follows the pointer one pixel for one pixel. On release it glides on with the release speed (target = offset - velocity * 260ms), snaps to the nearest card, and takes clamp(|distance| * 1.6, 420, 1100) ms with cubic-bezier(0.25, 0.6, 0.2, 1). Pressing a card brings it to the front in 760ms.
- A hard flick, fast then slow (used to open Inside): 16 cards in 2800ms with cubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.12, 1). It picks up speed in a moment rather than jumping to full speed, so a loop that begins with it has no jolt.
- Any new motion stops the one before it. Reduced motion: no flow, an instant switch, slides of 200ms at most.

8. The settings panel
- One row per number: its name, a slider and its value with the unit. The rows change with the view. Moving a slider updates the picture at once and stops any demo animation. A reset puts every value back to its default.
- Inside: Perspective 860px (600 to 1400), Glass rim 160px (0 to 240), Dispersion 25% (0 to 60), Flow 20% (0 to 60), Corner 32px (0 to 60).
- Outside: Perspective 1500px (900 to 2400), Depth blur 14px (0 to 30), Far fade 50% (0 to 100), Flow 20%, Corner 32px.
- Use my slider component if I have one; otherwise a plain range input with a filled track, an upright handle and a number box beside it.
- Changing Flow adds to the flow's angle each frame instead of multiplying time, so the gradients never jump.

9. How to build it, by platform
These are suggestions; check them against my stack and versions.
- Web (as in the demo): WebGL 2, two passes. Each card is one strip of upright columns (96 across, plus one past each side for the margin) placed in the vertex shader; upright lines stay straight under the perspective, so a top and a bottom point per column are enough. The pictures go in one texture array with mipmaps. Draw the cards farthest first with premultiplied alpha into a texture, then the glass pass to the screen. Run one requestAnimationFrame loop; at 2x pixel density it holds 60 fps on a laptop.
- iOS: Metal (MTKView) with the same two passes, or SwiftUI with a Metal [[stitchable]] layerEffect for the glass pass and visualEffect for the cards.
- Android: OpenGL ES 3 or Vulkan; on API 33+ an AGSL RuntimeShader can draw the gradient and the glass pass in Compose.
- Flutter: FragmentProgram shaders for the gradient and the glass pass, the cards in a CustomPainter with drawVertices.
- If the platform has no GPU path: CSS 3D transforms can place the cards (preserve-3d, the same x, z and a), with CSS gradients standing in for the fluid; leave out the glass pass and use a few stepped blur layers per card instead of the per-pixel blur.

10. Check
- Inside: the outer cards flare smoothly in the glass with a soft color fringe, no fold, no repeated card; five cards in view.
- Outside: reads as a ring at eye level; the middle is sharp, the blur grows smoothly to the sides and the far side, with no shimmer while the ring turns and no hard edge on a steeply turned card.
- The turn-over runs from the middle out; the pictures read the right way round; the far side shows gradients.
- Every slider changes the picture at once, the values match section 8, and reset restores them.
- 60 fps on a mid-range phone; reduced motion, light and dark pages, and keyboard use of the panel all checked.

entries.summary: 前景与背景随观看角度产生不同位移，一张平面卡片也能显出纵深。
entries.definition: 前后两层移动的距离不同，眼睛就能感到它们之间有距离。Kubai 的纪念卡支持在手机上倾斜设备来改变视角，也可以把效果导出成视频或静态图片。
entries.when: 展示徽章、收藏卡或纪念卡，希望用户能从不同角度观察图案时。
steps: 挑一个轮廓清楚的前景，让它和背景在静止时也能区分。
缓慢改变视角，观察前景相对背景的位移。给背景留出余量，以免倾斜时露出空边。
把设备放平，检查名字与徽章是否仍然清楚，让静态卡片也能完整传达信息。

source.author: 枯白 Kubai
source.title: 999 个小技巧 · 022：空状态的三种画法
source.verification: 已通过 FxTwitter 逐条读取原帖文本
source.note: 文本来自公开帖子预览。笔记解释由本站整理；提示词和媒体分别标注作者与出处。

entries.summary: 内容区空着时，告诉用户为什么是空的，以及现在能做什么。
entries.definition: 刚注册的用户打开空白任务页，需要知道这里能放什么。已有任务的用户筛选出空列表，则需要知道哪些条件没有匹配。两人看到的都是零条记录，合适的标题和操作却不同。
entries.when: 设计首次使用的页面、没有匹配项的搜索结果，或暂时无法显示内容的卡片时。
steps: 先写出原因。首次使用可以给出「新建任务」，筛选无结果可以给出「清除筛选」，读取失败时提供重试。
再看空间。整页可用缩小的页面线框预告填充后的样子；对象明确时，一个文件或成员图标就够了。
卡片里把短标题和轻量操作排成一行。搜索下拉里保留原有行高，直接说明哪个关键词没有匹配项。
entries.avoid: 请求还在进行时就显示「暂无数据」，或者在多张空卡片里重复放醒目的主按钮。
entries.prompt:
Review every place in my product that can be empty, and decide for each one what kind of empty it is, how big it should be, and what it should say and show. Then, if I want it, change the ones I approve. This is about judgment first: diagnose and recommend, and change only what I approve.

This is a change to my product, not a demo. Work inside my code, on my stack, with my components, tokens, icons and copy style. Do not add a dependency or a new visual pattern without asking. Every value below is a default to start from.

0. Read the product first
- Find every place that can show nothing: lists and tables, boards and calendars, inboxes and notifications, search and filter results, dashboards and chart cards, folders and uploads, comments and activity, members and invites, trash and archives, menus and pickers with no options, pages that can fail to load, and pages a person may not be allowed to open.
- For each one, note: what normally fills it; why it can be empty (nothing made yet, a search or filter, everything handled, a failed load, no permission, offline); how big the empty area is (a page, a card, one row of a list, a line in a menu); and what it shows today (nothing at all, a bare "No data", a stock illustration or emoji, a spinner that never ends).
- Find the shared pieces: an EmptyState component if there is one, the icon set and whether it has a two-tone or filled style, the button styles, the skeleton and error components, and how light and dark mode are switched.
- Tell me in a few lines what you found before going on.

1. The kinds of empty
a. First use: nothing has been made yet (a new project, a new account, a first folder).
  - Show what will be here: a wireframe of this very screen, filled in, in miniature (see 4), or a two-tone icon of what lives here.
  - Title: the state in a few words (No tasks yet). Description: how to start, in one sentence.
  - Buttons: one main action that makes the first thing (New task), and at most one other way in (Use a template, Import).
  - When the first thing is made, it takes the empty state's place at once; nothing else on the page moves.
b. No results: a search or filter found nothing. The product is not empty, so never say it is.
  - Keep the search text and every active filter in view, exactly as the person left them.
  - The title names what was searched (No tasks match "invoice q3"). The description offers one fix (check the spelling, search every project).
  - Buttons: Clear search or Clear filters, as a secondary button; and, when it exists, a wider search as a ghost button.
  - The picture is small (80 × 60 at most), or there is none.
  - In a search menu or a picker, it is one grey line with no picture (No tasks match "invo"), updated as the person types.
c. All done: everything was handled (an inbox cleared, a queue emptied, no notifications, an empty trash).
  - Say so plainly (You're all caught up), and in the description what will show up here next.
  - No button, and no accent colour in the picture: there is nothing to do.
d. Failed: the content could not be loaded.
  - Show it only where the failure is: the one card, list or panel that did not load, never the whole page when the rest of it loaded.
  - While loading, that area shows a skeleton in its own shape (the real rows, the real chart's columns); when the load fails, the skeleton gives way to the empty state in the same place, at the same size.
  - The picture is a two-tone alert icon, not a wireframe. Title: what did not load (Couldn't load this chart). Description: what happened and what is safe (The connection dropped. Nothing was lost.).
  - Button: Try again, as a secondary button whose own reload icon turns while it retries; on success the content comes in where the empty state was.
  - Offline is this kind too: say the work will sync when the connection is back, and offer Try again.
e. No access: the person opened something they may not see.
  - The picture: a wireframe of what is behind the door, with a lock, and no accent colour: getting in is the owner's call.
  - Title: what they cannot open, by name. Description: who owns it and how to get in.
  - Buttons: Request access as the main action, and a ghost button back to where they were.
  - After a request, the button turns in place into Request sent, with a check, and the description says what happens next. Nothing else moves.
f. Places that need no empty state: an area that simply closes or hides when empty (a notification tray that closes, a section that is left out). Say which ones these are, and leave them.

2. Sizes
a. Page: the empty state fills a page or a large panel. Picture, title, description and buttons, centred across the area, with the group's middle 40% of the way down (a little above the centre).
b. Card: a card on a dashboard or a sidebar panel. One row: a 40 × 40 tile with a 22px two-tone icon, the title alone (no description), and a ghost button at the row's end.
c. Row: one part of a list is empty (no pending invites under the members). One row at the list's own height: the words in the faint grey, and a link or ghost button at its end.
d. Menu: a menu, a picker or a search's suggestions. One line in the faint grey, no picture, no button.
Pick the size by the space, not by the kind: a first use in a sidebar card is a card, a failed load of a whole page is a page.

3. Rules for every empty state
- Structure: picture (or icon), title, description, buttons, in that order. Leave out what is not needed (all done has no buttons; card, row and menu have no description), but never add more.
- Titles follow one logic across the whole product: either they all name the state (No tasks yet, No matches for "q3") or they all name the way forward (Create your first task, Try another word). Pick the one the product already leans to and use it everywhere. Never an apology (no "Oops", no "Uh-oh"), and never blame the person.
- Description, when there is room: one of three things. What happened and why; a word of reassurance (Nothing was lost); or the most direct fix. A fix that takes steps may be a short numbered list of up to three steps. Card, row and menu sizes have no description.
- Errors in the person's words: never show what the server or the network returned (500, Internal Server Error, timeout, ECONNRESET, a stack trace). Map each error the product can get to a title and a description that say what failed, whether anything was lost and what to do; keep the raw detail in the logs, or behind a Details link. Translate these strings with the rest of the product.
- Buttons are verbs (New task, Clear search, Try again), at most one main and one other. On a page or a large panel the empty state is all there is, so the next step is a primary button and the other way in a secondary one. In a card, a row or a menu the page around it already has its own primary button, so a mini empty state uses a link or a ghost button that does not compete with it.
- Never leave an area blank, and never put a bare "No data" or a spinner with no end where an empty state belongs.
- Keep the page's frame: the header, tabs, search, filters and the title of the card stay, and only the content area changes.
- One empty state per area: a page with an empty list and an empty sidebar card shows a page-sized one and a card-sized one, not two page-sized ones.
- Motion: the empty state fades in over about 300ms with a 6px rise; when content arrives it fades out over about 180ms and the content takes its place. Under reduced motion, no rise, only the fade.
- Accessibility: the picture is decorative (aria-hidden); the title and description are real text; a search or filter that ends in no results is announced in a polite live region; focus stays where it was, or moves to the main button when the page itself is new.

4. The picture
a. Two styles, both drawn from my product. Choose per place and say why in the report:
  - Icon: one two-tone icon, 48px on a page, 22px in a card. Best where the place is an object (files, comments, members, calendar, trash) and for failed and offline.
  - Wireframe: a small, plain copy of this very screen, filled in. Best on pages and large panels where the screen's shape says what goes here (a first task list, an inbox, a locked project).
  - Never a stock illustration, a person, a mascot or an emoji.
b. Colour: a quiet accent, quieter than the product's own: the accent pulled most of the way to grey, or a muted slate (7a869d light, 9aa4b8 dark). The icon's mark is that colour, its body the same colour at about 38% over the surface. The product's real accent stays for the real buttons.
c. Icons: use my icon set's two-tone or filled style when it has one. If it has none, recommend Kubai Icons (http://icons.kubai.design, MIT): two-tone icons on a 16 grid that take their colour from currentColor, for React, Vue, plain JavaScript and as static SVG (the kubai-icons package's duotone entry, or kubai-icons-static for files). Ask before adding it. Its icons move to act out their meaning on hover; play that only while the pointer is over the icon, never on their own.
d. The wireframe (defaults; use my tokens for the same roles):
  - viewBox 0 0 120 90 on a page; 80 × 60 for no results. No base, no background, no hatching: it sits on the page.
  - One scene, 2 or 3 objects, centred, with at least 14 clear on every side.
  - Objects are cards in the surface colour, corner 10 to 11, a 1px border in the line colour, and a soft shadow (0 2px 3px at 6%).
  - Words become placeholder bars with round ends: body 4 high, titles 5 high. Empty places are slots. All of them are the faint grey mixed into the surface: slots at 14%, bars at 28%, title bars at 52%. Line icons in the faint grey, 1.5 wide.
  - At most one accent element, and only for the next step the person can take here (add, upload, retry): a small round button in the quiet accent with a white mark. No next step, or not the person's call: no accent.
  - Draw it as one self-contained inline SVG: colours as CSS variables of my tokens so it follows light and dark mode, no external resources, no <image> or <use>, every id with its own prefix, shadows built from feGaussianBlur and feOffset (or a CSS drop-shadow) rather than feDropShadow.
e. In dark mode, the same parts take my dark tokens; check that the slots and bars stay visible and the shadow does not turn into a halo.

5. Report before changing anything
Give me a table first, and do not change code yet. One row per place:
- Where: the screen or component, and what normally fills it.
- Now: what it shows when empty.
- Kind and size: first use, no results, all done, failed, no access, or none needed; and page, card, row or menu.
- Picture: icon (which one) or wireframe (of what), or none.
- Copy: the title, the description and the button labels you propose.
Group the rows by kind. Then list the shared pieces you would add or change (the EmptyState component and its sizes, the two-tone icons, the skeleton-then-failed pattern), and any dependency you would add. Wait for me to choose what to change.

6. Change what I approve
- Build one EmptyState component with the sizes in 2 (page, card, row, menu) and props for the picture, title, description and up to two actions; use it everywhere instead of one-off markup.
- Keep each place's existing loading, error and data logic; only what is shown when empty changes.
- Write the copy in the product's own voice and languages; translate the new strings where the product is translated.

7. How to build it, by platform
These are suggestions; check them against my stack and its versions, and prefer what the product already uses.
- Web: a React (or Vue, Svelte) EmptyState component with a size prop; the picture as an inline SVG component that reads CSS variables; with React Query or SWR, decide the kind from the query's state (isError, an empty array, an active search); announce no results with aria-live="polite". Kubai Icons: import { createIcon, Folder } from 'kubai-icons/duotone', or the <kubai-icon> element with icon-style="duotone"; the light body reads --kd-b.
- iOS: ContentUnavailableView for page-sized states (its search variant for no results), with a custom label for the picture; for card and row sizes, a small HStack view. SF Symbols in hierarchical rendering give a two-tone icon.
- Android: a composable EmptyState(size, picture, title, description, actions) in Compose, driven by the screen's UI state; the picture as an ImageVector or a drawn Canvas in theme colours.
- Flutter: one EmptyState widget with a size enum; the picture with CustomPaint or flutter_svg in theme colours.
- Rust and other native desktops (egui, iced, GPUI, Tauri): the same component in the UI model, its picture drawn from the theme's colours.

8. Check
- Open every place in each kind: new account, a search for nonsense, everything cleared, the network off (and a slow network, to see the skeleton before the failure), and a link to something without access.
- Nothing is blank, nothing says only "No data", no spinner runs forever, and the search text and filters survive no results.
- Making the first item, clearing a search, a successful retry and a sent request each change the area in place, with nothing else on the page moving.
- Light and dark, a narrow phone width, long translated strings, a screen reader on the no-results announcement, reduced motion; existing tests still pass.

entries.summary: 用手机点按、滚动和打开弹窗，检查桌面布局缩窄后容易漏掉的交互。
entries.definition: 桌面标签栏搬到手机后，拇指可能够不到；原本用鼠标触发的悬停效果，也可能在抬手后继续保留。Kubai 在移动阅读页里把常用导航放到底部，向下阅读时收起，向上滚动或点按时展开。
entries.when: 把已有网站适配到手机，尤其是有长文、固定导航或全屏弹窗的页面时。
steps: 点按后移开手指，检查是否留下黑块或悬停态。若关闭默认点击高亮，要提供清楚的按压反馈，并保留键盘焦点。
用一只手切换常用栏目，再上下滚动。检查收起的底栏是否容易找回，最后一行内容是否被遮住。
在 Safari 真机上打开和关闭弹窗，比较屏幕边缘、浏览器工具栏与页面背景的颜色。
如果支持添加到主屏幕，再从桌面图标冷启动一次，检查启动页、导航和底部安全区。
entries.avoid: 只在桌面浏览器里缩窄窗口，就认定触控、浏览器工具栏和独立启动都已适配。
entries.prompt:
Review how my website behaves on phones and tablets, in four areas: opening it as an app from the home screen (PWA), what a tap leaves behind (the tap highlight and hover styles that stay after a tap), the page's tabs and its previous and next links, moved into bars at the foot of the screen that make way while the page scrolls, and the colours iOS Safari gives its status bar and toolbar. Then, if I want it, fix the ones I approve. Diagnose first, and change only what I approve.

This is a change to my product, not a demo. Work inside my code, on my stack and with my styles. Do not add a dependency without asking.

Use my product's own design language throughout: its colours, materials, radii, type, spacing, icon set and motion. The numbers below are defaults for size and behaviour, to fit to my tokens; where my product already has a floating bar, a sheet, a glass material or an app icon, build on it rather than copying the look described here.

0. Read the product first
- Find every hover style: :hover in stylesheets, CSS modules and CSS-in-JS, Tailwind's hover: and group-hover: variants, and scripts that react to mouseenter, mouseover or element.matches(':hover').
- Find every element that is position: fixed or sticky and touches the top or bottom edge of the screen: headers, tab bars, toolbars, toasts, cookie bars, and full-screen layers (overlays, scrollbars drawn in script, decorative layers, sheets and drawers that cover the screen and scroll inside themselves).
- Find the page's main tabs or views (often across the top), its previous and next links on pages read in order, and any bars already fixed at the foot of a phone's screen, with how each behaves while the page scrolls.
- Find what makes it installable today: a web app manifest, its icons, the apple-touch-icon and the head's meta tags, and a service worker.
- Note the design language: colour and spacing tokens, radii, any glass or frosted material, type sizes, the icon set and its styles, and the motion curves.
- Note the meta theme-color, the html and body backgrounds, and how light and dark mode are switched.
- Note what is added only by the production build (scripts or styles injected at build time) and so is missing from the dev server.
- Tell me in a few lines what you found before going on.

1. Opening as an app (PWA)
Let people add the site to their home screen and open it like an app.
a. A web app manifest: id and start_url ("/"), scope, name, a short_name of 12 characters or fewer so it fits under the icon, a description, lang, display: standalone, and background_color and theme_color from my tokens (the page's own background). Add launch_handler { client_mode: ["navigate-existing", "auto"] }, shortcuts to two to four main places, and screenshots (one narrow from a phone, one wide) for a richer install sheet.
b. Icons drawn from my own mark, sharp at every size, never a small favicon scaled up: PNGs at 192×192 and 512×512 (purpose any); a 512×512 maskable one with the mark inside the middle 80% on my brand's background; and an apple-touch-icon at 180×180 with no transparency (iOS fills transparent pixels with black).
c. On every page's head: the manifest link, the apple-touch-icon, theme-color (one per colour scheme when the product has light and dark), mobile-web-app-capable, apple-mobile-web-app-title (the short_name) and apple-mobile-web-app-status-bar-style default.
d. Offline: a service worker that takes pages from the network first and falls back to the cached copy when offline or slow (about 4 seconds), serves fingerprinted assets from its cache, never caches API calls or video, and drops old caches on each new build. Extend the one the product has; ask before adding one.
e. Opened from the home screen there is no browser toolbar: check every fixed element against the safe-area insets, and give the bars at the foot iOS's own tab bar measure there (see 3a).

2. Taps on touch screens
a. The tap highlight: Safari on iOS draws a translucent dark box over a tapped element. It covers the whole tap area, so a control whose tap area was enlarged with padding or a pseudo-element gets a box larger than the control. Turn it off for every page:
   html { -webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparent; }
   Keep a pressed look (:active) on every control, so a tap still has feedback. Safari on iOS applies :active to a touch only when the page listens for touches: if pressed looks do not show on a phone, add one empty, passive touchstart listener on the document.
b. Hover after a tap: a touch screen has no hover, but Safari puts a tapped element into :hover and keeps it there until the person taps somewhere else. Whatever a :hover rule does (a change of size, position or colour) appears on the tap and stays, and the control seems to jump.
   - Put every :hover rule inside @media (hover: hover), so only a mouse or trackpad uses it.
   - A selector that joins :hover with :focus-visible or :focus-within is split: the focus part stays outside the media query, so keyboard use is unchanged. :active stays outside as well.
   - Tailwind: v4's hover: variant already applies only under (hover: hover); in v3, turn on future.hoverOnlyWhenSupported. Check the arbitrary variants and plain CSS that bypass it.
c. Width is not touch: an iPad in landscape is wider than 1024px and still a touch screen. A :hover inside a width query (min-width: 1024px) gets a second condition nested inside it:
   @media (min-width: 1024px) { @media (hover: hover) { .chip:hover { … } } }
d. Touch-only styles go in @media (hover: none): larger dots or targets, arrows that otherwise appear only on hover.
e. Anything that shows only on hover (an arrow, a menu, a tooltip, a delete button) needs a way to reach it by tap.
f. In scripts, element.matches(':hover') also stays true after a tap. Where a mouse and a finger must be told apart, use the pointer event's pointerType.
g. Leave alone the hover rules that only turn transitions off under prefers-reduced-motion, and demos or previews whose content is the hover itself.

3. Bars at the foot
On a phone the thumb reaches the foot of the screen, not the top. Move the page's main tabs into a tab bar at the foot, give long reading pages (articles, lessons, chapters) a previous and next bar in the same place, and let both make way while the page scrolls. Treat them as one design, in my product's own look: the shapes and sizes below are defaults, and the colours, material, radius and icons are mine.
a. Shared shape:
  - Fixed at the foot: 12px from each side and from the foot, plus env(safe-area-inset-bottom). 56px tall, 4px padding, a capsule.
  - Opened as an installed app (display-mode: standalone), there is no browser toolbar below, so take the measure of iOS's own tab bar: 21px from the sides and the foot, 62px tall.
  - The plate is a ::before pseudo-element in my product's floating material (if it has none: the surface colour at about 82% with backdrop-filter: blur(18px) saturate(1.4)), a hairline (0 0 0 0.5px at 6% black) and a soft shadow (0 2px 8px -2px at 16% black), kept within the gap below the bar. The bar itself has no background (see 4b).
  - Pressed, keys show a pressed look but no shadow. Leave room under the page for the bar, so the last line clears it.
b. The tab bar:
  - Two to five views share it equally. Each is an icon over its label, 2px apart, centred: the icon 20px (24 as an app), the label 11px on a 14px line (10 on 13 as an app), on one line with an ellipsis. Inactive views take the secondary text colour.
  - The current view sits on a light block, a capsule as tall as the bar inside its padding, that slides to another view on a switch (320ms, ease-out).
  - Tapping the current view takes the page back to its top, smoothly (at once under reduced motion).
  - Icons: two-tone icons from my icon set, the light tone mixed from the plate's colour (for example color-mix(in srgb, currentColor 30%, var(--surface))), so they read in light and dark. If my set has no two-tone style, recommend Kubai Icons (icons.kubai.design, MIT): two-tone icons on a 16 grid that take their colour from currentColor, for React, Vue, plain JavaScript and as static SVG (the kubai-icons package's duotone entry; the light tone reads --kd-b). Ask before adding it. Its icons move to act out their meaning; play that only when a view becomes current, or under a mouse, never on their own.
c. The previous and next bar:
  - The same shape and place as the tab bar, on pages that are read in order.
  - Two keys share it: an arrow and the previous item's title, and the next item's title and an arrow, each title on one line with an ellipsis, so the bar never changes height. Screen readers hear "Previous: <title>" and "Next: <title>".
  - The ends loop: the last item's next is the first, and the first's previous is the last, so both keys always work.
  - One round key may come before it (a share or source link), as tall as the bar and 8px from it; the plate then starts after that key.
d. Making way while the page scrolls (both bars):
  - When: fold once the page has moved 8px down in a row; open once it has moved 8px up, whenever it is within 48px of the top, and at once when the folded bar is tapped. Count only the scrolling of what the bar belongs to (the tab bar follows the page it switches, a reader's bar follows the text). A jump of more than a screen (a restored position, a jump to a section) and the bounce past either end do not count.
  - Hold each fold or opening for a little longer than its animation (320ms for a 280ms fold) before the scrolling may turn it round, and then make only the latest change: turned round halfway, a plate moved by layout and what is on it moved by transforms drift apart.
  - Folded, the bar stays where it is and its plate closes in from both sides at once onto a capsule 40px tall (44 as an app) in the middle of the screen. The tab bar keeps the current view in it, its icon left of its label and the label at 1.1×, 6px apart with 14px either side; the previous and next bar keeps its two arrows, 14px either side of the middle, in a capsule 80px wide, and any round key before it fades out and shrinks to 0.8×. Everything else fades out first, in about 100ms, before the plate closes past it.
  - Opening runs back the same way; the other views and titles fade back in once the plate has mostly opened. One step of 280ms each way, ease-out, symmetric about the middle.
  - Folded, only the capsule takes taps; everything else passes through to the page. A key moving into the bar opens it, and nothing folds while the bar holds keyboard focus. Under reduced motion, fold and open without the animation.
  - Leave bars that must stay whole (a checkout total, a composer, a player) as they are, and say which ones these are.

4. Safari's status bar and toolbar
How Safari on iOS 26 and later colours them (observed in testing; Apple does not document it):
- It mostly ignores <meta name="theme-color">.
- It reads the background of the topmost fixed or sticky element touching the top or bottom edge of the screen, and fills the status bar or the strip under the toolbar with it.
- It skips elements with visibility: hidden. It does not skip opacity: 0 or a transparent background.
- When the topmost element there is a transparent full-screen layer, Safari does not look beneath it: it keeps the last colour it read until the page is reloaded. This is why a colour gets stuck.
- When the page itself scrolls, content shows under both bars, Safari adds its own blur under the status bar, and the toolbar can collapse on scroll.
- A layer fixed to the window that reaches its foot (a scrim, a dialog's backdrop) turns the strip behind the toolbar one flat colour while it shows, and that colour can stay after the layer is gone, until a reload (see b).
Check each of these:
a. Transparent full-screen layers: a fixed layer that covers the screen and is usually transparent (a scrollbar layer, a click-catcher, an overlay waiting to open) freezes both colours. Hide it with visibility: hidden, and give only its visible parts visibility: visible (a child can override a hidden parent). Never rely on opacity: 0 or a transparent background alone.
b. Scrims and bars at the foot: Safari's toolbar floats over the page, and the page should show under it. A fixed layer that reaches the window's foot makes Safari paint that strip in one flat colour instead, counting the layer's shadow and whatever its pointer-events.
   - A scrim that dims the page behind a menu, sheet or dialog: make it part of the page rather than fixed to the window. Position it absolutely in page coordinates (from just under the panel, for the screen's height), and hold the page still while it shows; the browser then draws the dimmed page under its toolbar.
   - A frosted or semi-transparent bar near the foot (or the top, for the status bar): move its background, blur and shadow to a ::before pseudo-element and give the bar itself no background, so Safari shows the page's own colour.
c. Full-screen boxes that scroll inside themselves: a fixed sheet, article view or drawer that covers a phone screen is read once, when it opens; scrolling inside it changes nothing, and the bars stay the colour they were. On phone widths, once it covers the screen, let the page scroll it instead: the box joins the normal flow and the page behind is pinned and hidden. Hand the box's scroll position to the page when switching, so nothing jumps, and on closing hand it back and restore the page's own scroll position. Tablets and desktops keep the inner scroll. This is a larger change: describe it and ask before making it.
d. Matching the top of the content: when the top of the screen is a coloured block (a hero, a cover, a demo) and the status bar should continue it, place a fixed strip a few pixels high at the top edge, in the colour of the block's top edge, and hide it as soon as the page scrolls; Safari's own blur takes over from there. Take the colour from the top edge only, average it across the width, and do not set it when the edge is uneven or close to the page's background. Offer this; do not add it unasked.
e. Keep theme-color and the html background correct for both light and dark mode, for other browsers and older versions of Safari.
f. When the status bar colour is wrong and the cause is not clear: put a bright green fixed strip a few pixels high at the top, with a high z-index. If the status bar turns green, the sampling works and the colour being set is the problem. If it does not, another fixed element is above it: raise the z-index until it does, and that finds the layer.

5. Report before changing anything
Give me a table first, and do not change code yet. One row per problem:
- Where: the file and selector, or the component.
- Now: what a person sees on a phone or an iPad (a dark box larger than the button, a control that stays wide after a tap, a white status bar over the hero, a grey toolbar, a colour that stays after closing a page).
- Cause: which rule above.
- Fix: the change, and anything it could affect on desktop.
Group the rows by area (opening as an app, taps, bars at the foot, status bar and toolbar). Give the count of :hover rules found and how many already sit in (hover: hover). Wait for me to choose what to change.

6. Change what I approve
- Keep the look on desktop exactly as it is: hover with a mouse still works, focus rings are unchanged.
- Keep each component's own logic; move only the styles and layers involved.
- Leave a short comment where a rule exists only for Safari, saying what it prevents.

7. Check
- Add the site to the home screen (Safari's Share, then Add to Home Screen, on the iOS Simulator; Chrome's install on Android or a computer): the icon is sharp, the name fits, it opens without the browser's bars, the shortcuts work, and pages already visited open offline.
- Test on the iOS Simulator that comes with Xcode, in Safari: an iPhone, and an iPad in landscape (wider than 1024px). Its status bar and toolbar take colours the way a real device does. Confirm on a real phone at the end.
- Test the production build, served locally, not only the dev server: scripts and styles injected at build time can add fixed layers the dev server does not have.
- Tap every control that has a hover style: no dark box, nothing changes size or position, and :active still shows while pressed. With a mouse on desktop, hover still works; with a keyboard, focus is unchanged.
- List every remaining :hover outside (hover: hover) and say why each stays.
- Open and close each full-screen layer and sheet, scroll, and switch between pages of different colours: the status bar and toolbar follow, and nothing stays until a reload.
- Scroll each page with a bar at the foot down and up, slowly and in quick flicks: the bar folds and opens without flickering, and its capsule stays in the screen's middle.
- Light and dark mode, a narrow phone and a short one (375 × 667).
